desc: Sorcery of Adula, the Glintstone Dragon. Conjures a cold magic greatsword, then delivers a sweeping blow that launches a blade-like projectile of frost. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly. Adula, a devourer of sorcerers, was bested by Ranni and subsequently swore a knightly oath to her Dark Moon.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Moonlight Altar Acquired from defeating Glintstone Dragon Adula at the front entrance of the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
whatItIs: Casting it conjures a cold magic greatsword, then follows with a sweeping blow that launches a frost blade projectile. It is a Carian sorcery costing 22 FP and requiring 32 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The cold damage pairs well with Carian builds that already stack Intelligence, and the follow-up projectile keeps pressure on targets that try to sidestep the initial slash. A caster who has cleared the front of Manus Celes will find it a solid mid-range option for keeping groups at bay.
whenToUse: Equip it once the Intelligence investment supports the stat requirement and hold it for crowd fights where both the sweeping arc and the trailing projectile land. It drops as a guaranteed reward from defeating Glintstone Dragon Adula at the front entrance of the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
name: Adula's Moonblade
effect: Sweeping slash followed by cold blade projectile

desc: Superior incantation of Dragon Communion. Channels the power of the flying dragon Agheel. Transforms the caster into a dragon to spew flaming breath from above. This incantation can be used while jumping and charging extends the duration. The dead gazed at the skies over the lakes of Limgrave, praying that the dragons' flames would burn them to ash.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Flying Dragon Agheel.
whatItIs: Agheel's Flame transforms the caster into a dragon and spews flame breath from above. It is a Dragon Communion incantation costing 36 FP, needing 23 Faith and 15 Arcane, and charging extends the duration.
whyItMatters: The wide overhead flame area makes it a crowd-clearing tool for Faith-Arcane hybrid builds that lack heavy melee options. The dragon form also adds a vertical dimension to attacks, catching enemies that would otherwise duck under horizontal hits.
whenToUse: Cast it when a group of enemies clusters together and the overhead reach lets the flame catch everyone at once. It is acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Flying Dragon Agheel.
name: Agheel's Flame
effect: Spews flame breath of Agheel from above

desc: One of the night sorceries of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. Launches a projectile from a distance removed from the caster, so as to strike the enemy from behind. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly. The Sellian sorcerers were assassins, and it is said that they often hunted their fellows.
location: Loot: Weeping Peninsula Acquired from a corpse next to the imprisoned Sellen in the cellar of Witchbane Ruins.
whatItIs: The Night sorcery from Sellia launches a projectile from a distance removed from the caster so it strikes the target from behind. It costs 13 FP and requires 23 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The delayed origin point makes it deceptive in close-quarters fights where enemies expect a straight-line projectile. A low-Int build can slot it early without a heavy stat investment, and the cheap FP cost leaves room for other tricks in the same rotation.
whenToUse: Use it against single targets that lock onto the caster, since the projectile appears behind them rather than in front. It is looted from a corpse next to the imprisoned Sellen in the cellar of Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula.
name: Ambush Shard
effect: Strikes from behind with projectile fired from distance

desc: Sorcery of the servants of Death. Summons a horde of vengeful spirits that chase down foes. Charging enhances potency. They are cinders of the ancient death hex, raked from the fires of ghostflame by Deathbirds.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating the Death Rite Bird that roams the sunken ruins south of the Gate Town North Site of Grace at night.
whatItIs: The Death school sorcery summons a horde of vengeful spirits that chase down nearby foes. It costs 21 FP and demands 34 Intelligence plus 24 Faith; charging enhances the effect.
whyItMatters: The spirits home in on their targets, which makes it forgiving to land and effective against enemies that move erratically. A build mixing Intelligence and Faith gets a reliable crowd-control tool that does not depend on aim.
whenToUse: Release it when several enemies are within a moderate radius and the spirits can spread out to engage them individually. It is a guaranteed drop from defeating the Death Rite Bird that roams the sunken ruins south of the Gate Town North Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes at night.
name: Ancient Death Rancor
effect: Summons horde of vengeful spirits that chase down foes

desc: A secret incantation of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Creates a spear of red lightning and stabs it into the ground from above. On impact, the spear will burst into trails of lightning covering the area. Spoken of in legend, red lightning is the weapon wielded by the ancient dragons.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 8,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and...
whatItIs: A secret incantation of the dragon cult creates a spear of red lightning and stabs it into the ground from above. On impact the spear bursts into trails of lightning covering the area. It costs 25 FP and requires 32 Faith.
whyItMatters: The lightning trails punish enemies that stand still after the initial impact, making it effective in arenas where the boss does not keep moving. A pure Faith build gets a high-damage AoE without needing Arcane or any other secondary stat.
whenToUse: Aim it at a spot where the boss is about to charge or recover, so the trailing lightning catches them as they move through the zone. Buy it for 8,500 Runes from Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after handing either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
name: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear
effect: Stabs with red lightning spear from above

desc: A secret incantation of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons a red bolt of lightning that scatters and spreads around the surrounding area. Charging enhances the range of the lightning bolt. Spoken of in legend, red lightning is the weapon wielded by the ancient dragons.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 10,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and...
whatItIs: The chargeable companion summons a red bolt of lightning that scatters and spreads around the surrounding area. It costs 27 FP, needs 26 Faith, and charging extends the range.
whyItMatters: The spreading pattern covers a wider footprint than a single beam, which suits open arenas with multiple adds. A Faith build with moderate investment gets a reliable AoE that does not demand a full late-game stat dump.
whenToUse: Charge it before release when facing a spread-out group so the expanded radius catches more targets. Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Brother Corhyn will sell it for 10,500 Runes once either has received the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
name: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike
effect: Summons red lightning that spreads from impact

desc: Aspect of the Crucible discovered in the ancient ruins. Creates a miranda flower on one's chest before calling down a rain of light. Charging increases potency. In an age long past, before this land was enshrouded in shadow, the vitality of the Crucible flourished.
location: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom is found in the upper sections of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. From the Rauh Ancient Ruins, East site of grace, head across the bridge just to the west, then drop down to a slightly lower bridge section at the end.
whatItIs: An Erdtree incantation grows a miranda flower on the caster's chest before calling down a rain of light. It costs 23 FP, requires 27 Faith, and charging increases potency.
whyItMatters: The rain of light covers a wide area and hits everything underneath, making it useful against groups that close in from multiple angles. A Faith build gains a clean AoE that does not require a secondary stat and fits naturally into an Erdtree-focused rotation.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is needed to obtain this. Cast it when enemies cluster in the open and the falling light can hit all of them at once. It is found in the upper sections of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh: from the Rauh Ancient Ruins, East site of grace, head across the bridge just to the west, then drop down to a slightly lower bridge section at the end.
name: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom
effect: Creates a miranda flower on chest to summon rain of light

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Creates a throat pouch on the caster's neck, allowing them to spew fiery breath while walking. Charging increases the duration of the breath. This is a manifestation of the Erdtree's primal vital energies—an aspect of the primordial crucible, where all life was once blended together.
location: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath is acquired upon defeating Tanith's Knight, which can be fought after killing Tanith in Rykard's arena in the Volcano Manor, at the end of her questline.
whatItIs: A throat pouch appears on the caster's neck, allowing fiery breath to be spewed while walking. It is an ancient Erdtree incantation costing 28 FP, needing 27 Faith, and charging extends the duration.
whyItMatters: The mobile fire breath lets a caster deal continuous damage without committing to a stationary cast, which is valuable in fights against fast or dodging enemies. A Faith build gets a sustained-damage tool that works while repositioning.
whenToUse: Use it during the approach phase of a fight to chip away at an enemy's health before committing to a bigger attack. It is acquired upon defeating Tanith's Knight, which can be fought after killing Tanith in Rykard's arena in the Volcano Manor at the end of her questline.
name: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath
effect: Creates throat pouch to spew fire while walking

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Creates a mighty horn on the caster's shoulder to gore foes from a low stance. Charging allows the caster to barrel into foes before delivering the final attack. This is a manifestation of the Erdtree's primal vital energies—an aspect of the primordial crucible, where all life was once blended together.
location: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight in Stormveil Castle, down the outer western rampart. From the Rampart Tower Site of Grace, head north to the walkway with the Warhawks, and drop down to the left at the guard tower. Continue dropping down until you reach...
whatItIs: An ancient Erdtree incantation grows a mighty horn on the caster's shoulder for goring foes from a low stance. Charging lets the caster barrel into the target before the final hit lands. It costs 18 FP and requires 27 Faith.
whyItMatters: The forward lunge closes distance quickly, which suits fights against enemies that keep their range. A Faith build with a melee-oriented playstyle gets a punchy close-range attack that feels physical despite being a spell.
whenToUse: Charge it and barrel in when an enemy is staggered or recovering from their own attack, then deliver the horn into their guard. It is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight in Stormveil Castle, down the outer western rampart: from the Rampart Tower Site of Grace, head north to the walkway with the Warhawks, then drop down to the left at the guard tower and continue along the rampart.
name: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns
effect: Creates shoulder horn to gore foes from a low stance.

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Creates a supple tail that sweeps through foes before the caster. Charging enhances potency. This is a manifestation of the Erdtree's primal vital energies - an aspect of the primordial crucible, where all life was once blended together.
location: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight trapped in the Stormhill Evergaol, located in Stormhill.
whatItIs: A supple tail sweeps through foes in front of the caster when it is activated. It belongs to the wider Aspects of the Crucible group of Erdtree incantations, costs 20 FP, needs 27 Faith, and charging enhances the sweep's potency.
whyItMatters: The tail covers the space directly in front of the caster, which is useful for keeping close-range enemies at bay without turning around. A Faith build gets a quick, low-commitment attack that fits between longer casts.
whenToUse: Use it as a close-range counter when an enemy closes in from directly ahead, sweeping the area in front of you before they land a hit. Defeat the Crucible Knight trapped in the Stormhill Evergaol in Stormhill to add it to your repertoire.
name: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail
effect: Creates supple tail to sweep area before caster

desc: Aspect of the Crucible that manifested in golden hippopotami. Creates a bristling mass of thorn-like fur on the caster's back before scouring the area by rolling around on the ground. Charging increases the number of rolls and range of attack. In an age long past, before this land was enshrouded in shadow, the vitality of the Crucible flourished. Remains of this can be seen in the ancient ruins.
location: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns is acquired by defeating the Golden Hippopotamus boss found just inside the main gate of Shadow Keep on Scadu Altus.
whatItIs: Part of the Crucible family, it grows a bristling mass of thorn-like fur on the caster's back before scouring the area by rolling around. Charging adds more rolls and extends the range. It costs 14 FP and requires 27 Faith.
whyItMatters: The rolling movement makes it hard for enemies to track the caster, and the wide thorn path catches anything in the roll's trajectory. A Faith build gains a mobile AoE that covers ground while dealing damage.
whenToUse: This incantation cannot be learned without the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Use it in open spaces where the rolling path can cover a wide arc without hitting walls. It is acquired by defeating the Golden Hippopotamus boss found just inside the main gate of Shadow Keep on Scadu Altus.
name: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns
effect: Creates a mass of bristling thorns on back to scour the area

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' servants, who once served as the assassins of the Roundtable Hold. Completely silences the footsteps of the caster. Additionally, reduces fall damage and the sound produced by falling. This sorcery can be cast while in motion or crouching. The assassins were charged with eliminating Tarnished who had strayed from guidance.
location: Equipped: Assassin's Approach is a starting spell for the Confessor origin. Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 2,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the...
whatItIs: Assassin's Approach completely silences the caster's footsteps and also reduces fall damage and the sound produced by falling. It costs 15 FP, needs only 10 Faith, and can be cast while in motion or crouching.
whyItMatters: Silent movement lets a stealth-oriented build avoid aggro in areas where enemies are watching specific paths. The fall damage reduction is a small but welcome bonus for navigating vertical terrain without taking a hit.
whenToUse: Cast it before moving toward patrolling enemies or crossing open ground, then hold the crouch to stay silent while repositioning. It is a starting spell for the Confessor origin, and Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows also carry it for sale.
name: Assassin's Approach
effect: Silences footsteps, reduces fall damage / sound

desc: One of the incantations of Erdtree Worship. Greatly increases magic damage negation for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. This incantation was used by the champions of the Erdtree in the First and the Second Liurnian Wars, during which the red-haired Radagon joined the heroes' ranks.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Leyndell, Royal Capital Drops from an invisible Scarab rolling back and forth on the path patrolled by a Crucible Tree Knight, north of the Erdtree Sanctuary Site of Grace, past the elevator downwards. WARNING: If Maliketh, the Black Blade is defeated before this incantation is...
whatItIs: An Erdtree Worship buff that greatly increases magic damage negation for the caster and nearby allies. Holding the cast delays activation so a group can time it together. It costs 30 FP and requires 24 Faith.
whyItMatters: The magic resistance boost makes it a strong defensive tool against sorcery-heavy bosses and enemy spellcasters. A Faith build in a co-op session gets a force multiplier that protects the whole party.
whenToUse: Activate it right before a boss begins a heavy magic attack phase, or cast it while a co-op partner channels their own buff. It drops as a guaranteed reward from an invisible Scarab rolling back and forth on the path patrolled by a Crucible Tree Knight, north of the Erdtree Sanctuary Site of Grace in Leyndell, Royal Capital, past the elevator downwards; note that defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade before collecting it may make it unavailable.
name: Barrier of Gold
effect: Greatly increases magic damage negation for self & allies

desc: One of the greatest Dragon Communion incantations. Harnesses the fearsome power of Bayle the Dread. Channels the form of the dread dragon in the right arm to smash foes with an exposed talon bone coursing with flame lightning. Even after being consumed, the throbbing heart of Bayle continues to resist its subjugation, never weakening. One day, the fire within will consume the very body and soul of its Communion devourer. One day.
location: Dragon Communion: Foot of the Jagged Peak Trade the Heart of Bayle at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion. Mutually exclusive with Bayle's Tyranny, as the Heart of Bayle and its reward cannot be duplicated.
whatItIs: Bayle's Flame Lightning channels the form of Bayle the Dread in the caster's right arm to smash foes with an exposed talon bone coursing with flame lightning. It costs 43 FP, occupies two spell slots, and demands 53 Arcane.
whyItMatters: The close-range smash hits hard and the flame lightning adds a secondary damage type on top. An Arcane-heavy build gets a powerful melee-oriented spell that competes with dedicated weapons in burst damage.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Step in with it after a dodge or parry to punish an enemy that is committed to an attack. Trade the Heart of Bayle at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion at the Foot of the Jagged Peak to acquire it; note it is mutually exclusive with Bayle's Tyranny.
name: Bayle's Flame Lightning
effect: Channels dread dragon to strike with flame-lightning-infused talon bone

desc: One of the greatest Dragon Communion incantations. Harnesses the fearsome power of Bayle the Dread. Channels the form of the dread dragon to emit a mighty roar accompanied by a heatwave burst, causing violent eruptions of fire in the area. Even after being consumed, the throbbing heart of Bayle continues to resist its subjugation, never weakening. One day, the fire within will consume the very body and soul of its Communion devourer. One day.
location: Dragon Communion: Foot of the Jagged Peak Trade the Heart of Bayle at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion. Mutually exclusive with Bayle's Flame Lightning, as the Heart of Bayle and its reward cannot be duplicated.
whatItIs: Bayle's Tyranny emits a mighty roar accompanied by a heatwave, causing violent eruptions of fire across the area. It costs 46 FP, takes two spell slots, and requires 49 Arcane.
whyItMatters: The wide fire eruptions cover a large area and hit everything in the blast radius, making it a crowd-clearing tool. An Arcane build gets an AoE that does not depend on Faith or any secondary stat.
whenToUse: Hold it ready when a boss or a pack of enemies crowds a wide open arena, so the roar and the fire eruptions have room to scatter across the ground. It only shows up once the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is installed. The Grand Altar of Dragon Communion in the Foot of the Jagged Peak takes the Heart of Bayle as payment, which also locks out Bayle's Flame Lightning because the Heart cannot be duplicated.
name: Bayle's Tyranny
effect: Channels dread dragon to roar with a heatwave blast

desc: Incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Creates beast claws that rend the land with shockwaves. Charging enhances potency. This incantation represents the fury of Gurranq, his bestial nature returned, as much as it does his restless agitation.
location: Quest Item: Bestial Sanctum, Greyoll's Dragonbarrow Beast Claw is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the fifth Deathroot. (If Gurranq is hostile after consuming the fourth Deathroot, he may be calmed down by reducing his HP.)
whatItIs: Beast Claw creates beast claws that rend the land with shockwaves. It is a Bestial incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman, and charging enhances the damage. It costs only 10 FP with a Faith requirement of 8.
whyItMatters: The shockwave effect hits the ground, which catches enemies that would otherwise avoid a direct hit. A low-Faith build gets a solid melee-range attack without needing a high stat dump.
whenToUse: Swing it at the feet of a boss that is about to jump, so the shockwave catches the landing. Gurranq at the Bestial Sanctum in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow rewards it after receiving the fifth Deathroot.
name: Beast Claw
effect: Creates beast claws that tear through the land

desc: Incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Fills the body with bestial vigor, alleviating buildup of frost and blood loss. Having gained intelligence, the beasts must have felt how their wildness slipped away as civilization took hold.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Greyoll's Dragonbarrow Bestial Constitution drops from a Scarab near the western cliffs on the southern side of Farum Greatbridge.
whatItIs: Bestial Constitution fills the body with bestial vigor, alleviating both frost and blood loss buildup over its duration. It costs 10 FP and requires just 9 Faith.
whyItMatters: The resistance to frost and bleed makes it a reliable safety net for builds that face enemies with both status effects. A low-Faith build can afford to keep it equipped without worrying about the FP cost.
whenToUse: Cast it before entering an area known for frost or bleed enemies, such as the snow-capped sections of the Mountaintops. It drops from a Scarab near the western cliffs on the southern side of Farum Greatbridge in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.
name: Bestial Constitution
effect: Alleviates blood loss and frost buildup

desc: Incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Swiftly flings a number of sharp rock shards. This incantation can be cast without delay after performing another action. It is said that in the time before the Erdtree, stones were the first weapons of the beasts who had gained intelligence.
location: Quest Item: Greyoll's Dragonbarrow Bestial Sling is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the second Deathroot.
whatItIs: Bestial Sling swiftly flings a number of sharp rock shards. It is a fast Bestial incantation that can be cast without delay after another action, making it easy to chain. It costs 10 FP and needs only 7 Faith.
whyItMatters: The lack of cast delay means it can slot into any rotation without breaking the flow. A very low-Faith build gets a quick ranged option that does not demand a meaningful stat investment.
whenToUse: Use it to open a fight at range, softening the target before closing in. Gurranq in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow gives it once the second Deathroot has been handed over.
name: Bestial Sling
effect: Swiftly flings numerous sharp rock shards

desc: Incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Fills the body with bestial vigor, restoring HP over a period of time. Having gained intelligence, the beasts must have felt how their wildness slipped away as civilization took hold.
location: Quest Item: Bestial Sanctum, Greyoll's Dragonbarrow Bestial Vitality is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the third Deathroot.
whatItIs: Bestial Vitality fills the body with bestial vigor and restores HP over a period of time. It costs 18 FP and requires 12 Faith.
whyItMatters: The gradual healing makes it useful in sustained fights where a single flask charge would not cover the full duration. A low-Faith build gets a self-heal that does not require a high Faith investment or a dedicated healing item.
whenToUse: Cast it during a lull between exchanges while the gradual healing fills in, then press forward once your health has recovered enough to re-engage. It is given by Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum within Greyoll's Dragonbarrow once the required Deathroot has been handed over.
name: Bestial Vitality
effect: Restores HP over a period of time

desc: Power gleaned from the remembrance of Maliketh. Caster creates an illusory black blade, then leaps forward to deliver a spinning slash that emits a wave of light. This can be followed up with one additional attack. This blade was once imbued with Destined Death. In addition to dealing damage, it reduces foes' maximum HP and continues to sap their current HP for a very short time.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Black Blade, dropped by Maliketh, the Black Blade, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Black Blade creates an illusory black blade, then leaps forward to deliver a spinning slash that emits a wave of light. An additional attack can follow. It costs 26 FP, occupies two slots, and demands 46 Faith.
whyItMatters: The HP reduction effect weakens even the most enduring bosses over the course of a fight, making it a force multiplier in long encounters. A high-Faith build gets a tool with an effect that sets it apart from standard damage spells.
whenToUse: Leap in with it when a boss is staggered and the spinning slash plus follow-up can land in quick succession. Trade the Remembrance of the Black Blade, dropped by Maliketh, the Black Blade, with Finger Reader Enia to acquire it, or duplicate one using a Wandering Mausoleum.
name: Black Blade
effect: Black blade spinning slash that emits wave of light

desc: A black flame incantation of the Godskin Apostles. Throws a ball of raging black fire. Charging enhances potency and causes the fireball to explode. Black flame is weighty. After dealing damage, it continues to sap foes' HP for a very short time.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Godskin Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have...
whatItIs: Hurls a heavy ball of black fire that, on impact, detonates and then continues to drain the target's HP for a brief moment. Holding the cast button before release makes the fireball larger and more powerful. It costs 18 FP and requires 20 Faith.
whyItMatters: The lingering drain after the initial hit makes it especially effective against high-HP bosses, and the ranged cast keeps the caster at a safe distance. A Faith build can pick it up early and use it as a reliable opener without needing a melee kit to complement it.
whenToUse: Equip it as soon as Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows lists it in their shop after receiving the Godskin Prayerbook, which sells for 7,500 Runes in Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or Mountaintops of the Giants. Fire it at any boss with a long health bar and step back while the drain ticks.
name: Black Flame
effect: Throws a ball of raging black fire

desc: A black flame incantation of the Godskin Apostles. Engulfs Armament held in the right hand with black flame. This incantation can be cast without delay after performing another action. Black flame is weighty. After dealing damage, it continues to sap foes' HP for a very short time.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 6,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Godskin Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have...
whatItIs: Wraps the right-hand weapon in black flame for a short duration, so every subsequent melee hit deals fire damage and continues to drain the target's HP. It costs 15 FP and requires 17 Faith. The cast can follow immediately after another action, making it seamless in a combo.
whyItMatters: A Faith build that still wants to swing a weapon gets both worlds from this buff: black flame damage layered on top of physical hits, plus the lingering HP drain after each contact. It is cheap in FP, easy to slot into any melee rotation, and works with any right-hand weapon.
whenToUse: Hand the Godskin Prayerbook to either Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows, and Black Flame Blade is then sold from any of their posts, whether that is the Mountaintops of the Giants, Leyndell, Royal Capital, Altus Plateau, Liurnia of the Lakes, or back at Roundtable Hold. Cast it right before you strike so the opening hit already carries black flame and the foe keeps losing health for a moment after the blow lands. A hybrid build that mixes physical weapon damage with flame wants a slot open for it.
name: Black Flame Blade
effect: Enchants right-hand armament with black flame

desc: Superior black flame incantation of the Godskin Apostles. Summons a circle of black flame pillars around the caster. Charging increases the size of the circle. The Gloam-Eyed Queen led the apostles. It is said that she was an Empyrean chosen by the Fingers.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Mountaintops of the Giants Black Flame Ritual is received upon defeating the Spiritcaller Snail boss in Spiritcaller Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This Snail summons the spirits of a Godskin Apostle and a Godskin Noble.
whatItIs: Summons a ring of black flame pillars that erupt around the caster, and holding the cast button before release expands the radius of the circle. It demands 30 FP and 42 Faith, placing it firmly in late-game territory. The black flame continues to drain HP after each pillar strikes.
whyItMatters: A wide-area burst is invaluable in tight spaces or against groups that close in from multiple angles, and the drain effect keeps pressure on any boss standing inside the ring. A late Faith build that has outgrown single-target fireballs gains a crowd-clearing and zone-control tool.
whenToUse: Defeat the Spiritcaller Snail boss in Spiritcaller Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants to receive it as a guaranteed drop. Use it when surrounded in a narrow arena or when a boss is locked in a multi-phase pattern and needs a wide hit to break concentration.
name: Black Flame Ritual
effect: Summons a circle of black flame pillars around caster

desc: A black flame incantation of the Godskin Apostles. Summons black fire within, increasing physical damage negation. However, sacred flasks and other such forms of HP restoration are impaired. The Apostles were all embraced by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, and the black flame was their armor within.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold Acquired from Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after selecting the "about the secret medallion" dialogue option. This option will only appear after the player has obtained both the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) and Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
whatItIs: A defensive incantation that calls black fire inward to raise physical damage negation for as long as the buff lasts. It costs 30 FP and requires 30 Faith. The trade-off is that sacred flasks and other forms of HP restoration are weakened while it is active.
whyItMatters: Physical damage reduction is one of the most forgiving buffs in the game, turning hits that would otherwise be one-shots into survivable exchanges. A melee-leaning Faith build benefits the most, since it can stay in the fight longer and treat the weaker flask as a minor inconvenience.
whenToUse: Acquire it from Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing in Roundtable Hold after selecting the "about the secret medallion" dialogue option, which only appears once both the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) and Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left) are in the inventory. Equip it before a boss that hits hard with physical attacks and accept the weaker flasks as the trade.
name: Black Flame's Protection
effect: Increases physical damage negation

desc: Gravity-manipulating sorcery of Commander Gaius. Pulls blade-like clumps of rock from the earth. Charging increases potency. Gaius and Radahn were good rivals in their youth, and this sorcery is a product of their friendly competition.
location: Trade: Finger Reader Enia Defeat Commander Gaius and trade his Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia.
whatItIs: Rock shards rip upward from the ground in a fan that arcs ahead of the caster. Holding the cast button through the release window amplifies how far each blade travels and how hard it lands. It demands a high Intelligence score and a chunk of FP, so a caster who has grown into late-game stats will notice the hit the most.
whyItMatters: The fan of rock blades covers a wide horizontal arc, making it effective against groups and against bosses that lunge into the caster's space. A late Intelligence build that wants a melee-range sorcery without committing to a staff swing finds a reliable gap-filler here.
whenToUse: Learning this sorcery is gated behind the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Defeat Commander Gaius and trade his Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia to receive it. Fire it when a boss telegraphs a ground-slam or when several enemies converge from the same direction.
name: Blades of Stone
effect: Summons rock blades from the earth

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Grants a greater blessing to the caster and nearby allies, gradually restoring a large amount of HP. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. The Erdtree once flourished with abundance—yet it was only for a fleeting moment. Such is the course of all life.
location: Loot: Leyndell, Royal Capital Blessing of the Erdtree is located near the Queen's Bedchamber Site of Grace in Leyndell, on the Altus Plateau. WARNING: This item is no longer obtainable after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.
whatItIs: An Erdtree incantation that grants a powerful healing aura to the caster and any nearby allies, restoring a large amount of HP over time while the channel holds. It costs 60 FP and requires 38 Faith, and the activation can be delayed by holding the cast button before release.
whyItMatters: A strong, sustained heal that covers the caster and allies makes it the go-to emergency recovery in tough fights where a single flask is not enough. A high-Faith build benefits most, since the 60 FP cost is a meaningful fraction of a typical pool.
whenToUse: Pick it up near the Queen's Bedchamber Site of Grace in Leyndell, Royal Capital on the Altus Plateau, and collect it before defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, since it disappears from the world afterward. Channel it during a boss's multi-hit combo when the HP bar is dropping fast and a single flask will not close the gap.
name: Blessing of the Erdtree
effect: Grants greater blessing to self and nearby allies

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Grants a blessing to the caster and nearby allies, gradually restoring HP. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. Blessings once fell like tears from the Erdtree, and this incantation is but a lingering remnant of their power.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes Blessing's Boon is sold by Miriel, Pastor of Vows for 4,000 Runes. Should Miriel die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Miriel's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: A lingering Erdtree blessing that settles over the caster and any nearby allies, mending wounds bit by bit over a short window. Holding the cast button through the prayer delays the moment it springs into effect, letting the caster line up the timing. It asks for a solid Faith score and a moderate FP spend per activation.
whyItMatters: A moderate, sustained heal that does not demand a high Faith investment makes it accessible to hybrid builds that split points between Faith and another stat. It is an earlier and more affordable option in the Erdtree healing line, covering the same ally-healing role at a lower stat gate.
whenToUse: Buy it from Miriel, Pastor of Vows for 4,000 Runes in Liurnia of the Lakes, or claim it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price by handing over Miriel's Bell Bearing if Miriel has already died. Hold it during a prolonged fight when the HP bar is steadily eroding and a single flask will not hold.
name: Blessing's Boon
effect: Grants blessing to self and nearby allies

desc: Sacred incantation of Mohg, Lord of Blood. Thrust arm into the body of the Formless Mother, then scatter the bloodflame to set the area ablaze. This incantation can be cast while in motion. The mother of truth craves wounds. When Mohg stood before her, deep underground, his accursed blood erupted with fire, and he was besotted with the defilement that he was born into.
location: Trade: Finger Reader Enia Trade the Remembrance of the Blood Lord, dropped by Mohg, Lord of Blood, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Scatters bloodflame in an area before the caster, setting the ground ablaze and dealing damage to anything that crosses through it. It costs 13 FP and requires 14 Faith and 17 Arcane. The cast can be performed while moving, so it slots naturally into a roll or dodge.
whyItMatters: A cheap, mobile area attack is ideal for kiting enemies in corridors or punishing pursuers who chase too aggressively. A Faith-Arcane build gets a reliable ground effect that does not require standing still, and the bloodflame continues to build blood loss on contact.
whenToUse: Trade the Remembrance of the Blood Lord, dropped by Mohg, Lord of Blood, with Finger Reader Enia to receive it, or duplicate one in a Wandering Mausoleum for a single copy per playthrough. Drop it behind the caster while retreating through a narrow passage so the flame covers the ground just vacated.
name: Bloodboon
effect: Scatters bloodflame before caster to set area aflame.

desc: A Blood Oath incantation, granted by the Lord of Blood. Engulfs armament held in the right hand with bloodflame. This incantation can be cast while in motion. After dealing damage, bloodflame continues to build up onset of blood loss for a very short time.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Drops from a Scarab northwest of Rose Church.
whatItIs: Coats the weapon in the right hand with a seeping bloodflame that, after each hit lands, keeps draining the target's health for a brief moment. It can be cast while still moving, so a caster mid-strike or mid-dodge can layer it on without breaking rhythm. The stat requirements lean toward Faith with a touch of Arcane, and the FP cost sits in the moderate range.
whyItMatters: Blood loss scales with the target's maximum HP, which makes a modest weapon hit feel disproportionately punishing against bosses. A hybrid Faith-Arcane build that swings a weapon gains a build-defining enhancement without giving up melee, and the low stat gates mean it is usable early.
whenToUse: Find it as a guaranteed drop from a Scarab northwest of Rose Church in Liurnia of the Lakes. Apply it before engaging any boss with a large health bar so the blood loss ticks accumulate over the fight.
name: Bloodflame Blade
effect: Enchants right-hand armament with bloodflame

desc: A Blood Oath incantation, granted by the Lord of Blood. Creates bloodflame lacerations before the caster, which explode in an instant. This incantation can be cast repeatedly. After dealing damage, bloodflame continues to build up onset of blood loss for a very short time.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Subterranean Shunning-Grounds Acquired from defeating Mohg, the Omen at the Cathedral of the Forsaken.
whatItIs: Creates a burst of bloodflame lacerations that appear in front of the caster and detonate almost instantly. It costs 12 FP and requires 13 Faith and 15 Arcane. The cast can be repeated in quick succession, making it function like a rapid-fire close-range burst.
whyItMatters: A fast, repeatable close-range attack covers the gap when a boss is in the caster's face and a charged shot is not practical. The bloodflame also builds blood loss on contact, adding pressure on high-HP targets. A Faith-Arcane caster gains a dependable panic button that costs very little FP per activation.
whenToUse: Defeat Mohg, the Omen at the Cathedral of the Forsaken in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds to claim it. Tap it repeatedly when a boss closes to melee range and a charged incantation would leave the caster exposed.
name: Bloodflame Talons
effect: Creates bloodflame lacerations that then explode

desc: Superior incantation of Dragon Communion. Channels the power of Borealis the Freezing Fog. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew icy breath from above. Charging extends duration. This incantation can be cast while jumping. The ice dragons were once lords of the mountaintops long ago, until they were defeated by the Fire Giants and chased from the peak.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog on the Mountaintops of the Giants.
whatItIs: Transforms the caster into a dragon for a short time and spews a wide cone of freezing breath downward from above. It costs 48 FP and requires 23 Faith and 15 Arcane, and holding the cast button extends the duration of the breath. The spell can be cast while jumping, which is how most casters will actually use it.
whyItMatters: A wide, lingering frost cone is excellent against groups and against bosses that stay in one spot, because the breath covers a large area and the freezing effect slows the target. A Faith-Arcane build that wants a flashy area denial tool without committing to a staff gets it here.
whenToUse: Acquire it from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts, but only after defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog on the Mountaintops of the Giants. Jump and release it over a clustered group of enemies or a stationary boss to blanket the area in frost.
name: Borealis's Mist
effect: Spews icy breath of Borealis from above

desc: An aberrant sorcery discovered by exiled criminals. Theirs are the sorceries most reviled by the academy. Wounds the caster with thorns of punishment, sending a trail of bloodthorns running over the ground to impale enemies from below. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly. The guilty, their eyes gouged by thorns, lived in eternal darkness. There, they discovered the blood star.
location: Loot: Mountaintops of the Giants Located by a dead tree on the western cliffs of the southern end of the giant stone bridge surrounded by Guilty enemies.
whatItIs: Wounds the caster with thorns and sends a trail of bloodthorns skittering across the ground to impale enemies from below. It costs 9 FP and requires 21 Faith. The cast can be repeated, so the trail can be extended by firing it multiple times in a row.
whyItMatters: A ground-level attack is one of the few ways to hit enemies that float, fly, or stand at a height the caster cannot reach with a normal swing. It costs very little FP and requires only Faith, so a low-level caster or a hybrid build can carry it as a situational tool without sacrificing a better slot.
whenToUse: Find it by a dead tree on the western cliffs of the southern end of the giant stone bridge on the Mountaintops of the Giants, surrounded by Guilty enemies. Fire it at the feet of flying or elevated enemies that a straight-line attack cannot reach.
name: Briars of Punishment
effect: Wounds caster to unleash a trail of bloodthorns

desc: An aberrant sorcery discovered by exiled criminals. Theirs are the sorceries most reviled by the academy. Wounds the caster with thorns of sin, creating a spiral of bloodthorns. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly, up to three times. The guilty, their eyes gouged by thorns, lived in eternal darkness. There, they discovered the blood star.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Obtained by defeating a lone Guilty located southwest of the Fire Monk Campsite, near the Church of Vows in Liurnia. This Sorcerer is near a group of Fire Slugs to the north of the Artist's Shack (Liurnia).
whatItIs: Spins a spiral of bloodthorns around the caster's own blood, creating a short-range burst that damages anything nearby. It costs 6 FP and requires 24 Faith. The cast can be repeated up to three times, building the spiral outward with each activation.
whyItMatters: An ultra-cheap close-range burst is a reliable panic option when a surprise enemy closes the gap and the caster has nothing better queued. The three-charge cap means it can be dumped in a single combo without worrying about FP, and the 24 Faith gate is low enough for early hybrid builds.
whenToUse: Defeat a lone Guilty southwest of the Fire Monk Campsite, near the Church of Vows in Liurnia of the Lakes, to claim it. The enemy sits near a group of Fire Slugs to the north of the Artist's Shack. Tap it when ambushed in a tight space and a charged cast is not an option.
name: Briars of Sin
effect: Summons thorns from a whorl of your own blood

desc: One of the incantations that draws directly from the power of the Fire Giants. Raises a series of flame pillars around the caster. Charging further increases the number of flame pillars. The Fire Giants borrowed from the power of a fell god, and still they were defeated. Yet their failure released them from their solitary curse: to serve as keepers of the Flame for eternity.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Fire Giant, gained by defeating the Fire Giant, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: A ring of fire pillars erupts from the ground around the caster, engulfing everything in a wide circle. The longer the cast button is held before release, the more pillars break through the earth and the wider the zone becomes. It demands a high Faith score and a moderate FP cost per use.
whyItMatters: A 360-degree burst is the answer to a surround or a room full of melee enemies, because no single directional attack can cover all angles at once. A Faith build that is comfortable staying mobile gains a crowd-clearing tool that also punishes bosses dashing into the caster's personal space.
whenToUse: Defeat the Fire Giant, then hand his Remembrance of the Fire Giant to Finger Reader Enia in exchange for the sorcery. A Wandering Mausoleum can also produce a copy, though a playthrough allows a single one from either source. Cast it the instant a crowd of enemies closes within melee range and a backpedal is no longer an option, since the pillar ring catches anyone standing close.
name: Burn, O Flame!
effect: Raises a series of flame pillars around caster

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Lobs an explosive magic projectile that flies in an arc. Charging enhances potency. Drawn from the conspectus of Haima, the adjudicator of the academy, this sorcery employs might as a means to quell conflict.
location: Converted Fringe Tower, north-east Liurnia of the Lakes, not to be mistaken with the Converted Tower in the south-west. You will need to use the Erudition gesture given by Thops in front of the statue of Marika. This will reveal a hidden ladder to the top of the tower with a treasure chest that...
whatItIs: Lobs an explosive magic projectile in a high arc that detonates on impact, dealing area damage at the landing point. It costs 38 FP and requires 25 Intelligence, and holding the cast button before release increases the size and damage of the blast. It is a Glintstone sorcery from the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
whyItMatters: A lobbed projectile that explodes on arrival is useful against bosses that sit behind cover, crouch, or have a low profile that a straight-line bolt would sail over. An Intelligence build that wants a reliable area nuke without the commitment of a charged sorcery gets a dependable option at a moderate FP cost.
whenToUse: Locate it in the Converted Fringe Tower north-east of Liurnia of the Lakes, not the Converted Tower in the south-west, by using the Erudition gesture given by Thops in front of the statue of Marika to reveal a hidden ladder to a treasure chest at the top. Aim the arc over a boss that is crouching or sheltering behind an obstacle.
name: Cannon of Haima
effect: Lobs an explosive magic projectile in an arc

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Conjures a magic greatsword and then delivers a sweeping blow. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 10,000 Runes by Miriel, Pastor of Vows. Should Miriel die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Miriel's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: Conjures a magic greatsword and delivers a sweeping horizontal blow that covers a wide arc in front of the caster. It costs 12 FP and requires 24 Intelligence. The cast can be repeated, so a quick double-swing is possible before the FP cost becomes a concern.
whyItMatters: A mid-range sweep with decent reach and low FP cost makes it a versatile default for an Intelligence build that does not yet have a preferred attack pattern. It covers more ground than a straight bolt and less than a full-area burst, filling the middle slot in a sorcerer's kit.
whenToUse: Miriel, Pastor of Vows sells it in Liurnia of the Lakes or at Roundtable Hold, and the Twin Maiden Husks take over the sale once Miriel's Bell Bearing has been handed in. Slot it in during the Liurnia stretch as a dependable mid-range slash, then swap it out once a preferred sorcery earns the place. The low FP spend lets a caster swing it between dodges without watching the bar drain.
name: Carian Greatsword
effect: Performs sweeping slash using magical greatsword

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Creates a defensive arch of numerous magic glintblades overhead, which automatically attack nearby foes. This sorcery can be used cast while in motion. An enhanced version of the glintblade sorcery used by enchanted knights.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 12,000 Runes by Preceptor Seluvis. Should Seluvis die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Seluvis's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: Forms a defensive arch of numerous magic glintblades overhead that automatically seek and strike nearby enemies for a short duration. It costs 24 FP and requires 34 Intelligence. The spell can be cast while moving, so it does not require the caster to stand still.
whyItMatters: An auto-attacking blade shield is a passive damage source that punishes enemies for closing in, which is exactly the situation where a sorcerer is most vulnerable. A mid-tier Intelligence build gets a self-sufficient defense that costs one FP expenditure and then works on its own.
whenToUse: Preceptor Seluvis has it for sale in Roundtable Hold or Liurnia of the Lakes, and if he is already dead the Twin Maiden Husks will part with it after Seluvis's Bell Bearing is given over. Activate it the moment a boss closes to melee range and the caster needs to keep pressing forward without standing still. The overhead blades keep biting even while dodging, which makes it a strong choice against aggressive melee opponents.
name: Carian Phalanx
effect: Forms a defensive arch of numerous magic glintblades

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Conjures a magic greatsword to impale foes. Charging lengthens the initial step in. This sorcery forms a counterpart to Carian Greatsword. Highly lethal when used against single foes riding alone.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from felling a Scarab in Caria Manor, located in the lowermost courtyard full of fingercreepers northeast of Main Caria Manor Gate, near a crystal formation.
whatItIs: Sends a magic sword forward in a straight line to impale a single target, and holding the cast button before release lengthens the initial forward lunge. It costs 17 FP and requires 27 Intelligence. It forms a counterpart to Carian Greatsword, trading the wide sweep for a focused piercing strike.
whyItMatters: A single-target piercing attack is effective against bosses that ride alone or stand in a narrow corridor where a wide swing would miss. An Intelligence build that wants a reliable one-hit-burst against a single target gets a clean, focused tool that rewards good timing.
whenToUse: Fell a Scarab in Caria Manor to claim it, located in the lowermost courtyard full of fingercreepers northeast of Main Caria Manor Gate, near a crystal formation. Fire it at a lone boss or a single elite enemy when a straight line to the target is clear.
name: Carian Piercer
effect: Conjures a magic sword to impale foes

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Swing your staff to dispel incoming sorceries and incantations, using their power to retaliate with glintblades. This was the Carian royal family's secret means to prepare against the disloyalty of the academy. The moon and stars would one day go their separate ways.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 9,000 Runes by Preceptor Seluvis. Should Seluvis die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Seluvis's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: Swing the staff to intercept an incoming sorcery or incantation mid-flight, and the blocked power immediately turns into a volley of glintblades cutting back at whoever fired it. A Carian royal-family sorcery, it asks for a fair Intelligence score and a small FP cost per use. The window is tight: the staff swing must meet the projectile while it is still traveling, so the cast has to be timed against a visible incoming bolt.
whyItMatters: A free counter-attack that also negates the enemy's spell turns a defensive moment into an offensive one, and the skill ceiling is high enough to feel rewarding when it lands. A low-level Intelligence build or any caster facing a sorcerer enemy can use it as a cheap insurance policy, since 8 FP is a small ask.
whenToUse: Preceptor Seluvis stocks it at both Roundtable Hold and Liurnia of the Lakes, and the Twin Maiden Husks step in as sellers once Seluvis's Bell Bearing is delivered. Swing the staff the instant a glowing enemy projectile crosses into range, because the retaliation fires the moment the incoming spell is dispelled. It shines in duels against enemy sorcerers and incanters who lean on slow, telegraphed bolts.
name: Carian Retaliation
effect: Dispels enemy spells and retaliates with glintblades

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Conjures a magic sword and delivers a swift sweeping slash. This sorcery can be used without delay after performing another action. Even among the Carian sword sorceries, this is a notably effective technique.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold Sold for 1,500 Runes by Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Preceptor Seluvis after giving either of them the Royal House Scroll. Should the scroll be given to one of them and then have that instructor...
whatItIs: Carian Slicer conjures a magic sword that arcs in a wide horizontal slash across everything in a narrow band ahead. Because the cast has no recovery delay, it slots directly after a dodge or a basic attack with no gap, making it a natural follow-up in a combo string. It needs only a low Intelligence floor and a very small FP outlay per use.
whyItMatters: A near-free attack that slots into any combo without pausing makes it the default filler for a new Intelligence build that has just picked up a staff. The 4 FP cost means it can be spammed in quick succession, and the no-delay cast keeps the rhythm of a melee-like rotation intact.
whenToUse: Buy it from Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows, or Preceptor Seluvis for 1,500 Runes in Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, the Academy of Raya Lucaria, or Roundtable Hold after handing one of them the Royal House Scroll. Use it as the go-to attack from the first hour until a preferred sorcery takes the slot.
name: Carian Slicer
effect: Performs swift sweeping slash using magical sword

desc: Incantation originating from a sinister prophecy. Momentarily sparks flame from the caster's hand. This incantation can be cast without delay after performing another action. The flame of ruin is anathema to the Erdtree. But prophets sometimes glimpse it within the faith all the same. Sadly when this occurs their sole reward is banishment.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 600 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them...
whatItIs: An incantation that sparks a burst of flame from the hand for a moment. It costs 10 FP and asks for 8 Faith, and it can be thrown right after another action with no delay.
whyItMatters: The flame does little on its own, but the no-delay cast lets it slot into a melee combo as a quick poke. A Faith build wanting a cheap offensive spell between hits has a home here.
whenToUse: Buy it for 600 Runes from Brother Corhyn, who sells it in Roundtable Hold, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and Mountaintops of the Giants, or from the Twin Maiden Husks if Brother Corhyn is dead. Equip it early on a Faith build for a fast, reliable jab.
name: Catch Flame
effect: Momentarily sparks flame from hand

desc: A finger sorcery of Count Ymir, aspiring mother of fingers. Surrounds the caster with a mesh of hefty fingers that wards all manner of projectiles, whether magical or physical in nature, away from the caster. Charging enhances potency. The dear fingers look after their mother, or perhaps that is merely what the mother wishes to believe.
location: Loot: Scadu Altus Found in the small graveyard attached to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr after completing Count Ymir's questline.
whatItIs: It surrounds the caster with a mesh of hefty fingers that deflects both magical and physical projectiles away. It costs 20 FP and needs 36 Intelligence, and holding the charge makes the barrier stronger.
whyItMatters: It turns the caster into a moving shield against arrows, bolts, and enemy spells, which is useful in any fight where ranged attacks dominate. A caster who must cross open ground or soak a volley while repositioning will reach for it.
whenToUse: This spell has no source outside the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. After finishing Count Ymir's questline, it is looted from the small graveyard attached to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr in Scadu Altus, and it suits a caster build facing projectile-heavy fights.
name: Cherishing Fingers
effect: Surrounds the caster with a mesh of hefty fingers

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries that manipulates gravitational forces. Fires numerous gravitational projectiles. Any foes struck will be pulled toward the caster. Charging enhances potency. A gravitational technique mastered by the young Radahn. "I thank you for your tutelage, for now I can challenge the stars."
location: Loot: War-Dead Catacombs Acquired from a treasure chest in the middle of the scarlet swamp water in the lower levels of the large hall where all the phantoms are fighting each other.
whatItIs: A gravity sorcery that fires a volley of projectiles and yanks struck foes toward the caster. It costs 18 FP and wants 36 Intelligence, and the charge adds more force.
whyItMatters: Pulling an enemy inward is handy for closing gaps, for dragging a big foe toward an edge, and for baiting a heavy swing to miss. A caster fighting from range who wants to control spacing will like the hook.
whenToUse: Open the treasure chest sitting in the scarlet swamp water at the lower level of the large hall in War-Dead Catacombs, where the phantoms fight each other, and it is inside. It fits a mid-Intelligence caster who wants a crowd-control trick before heavier sorceries come online.
name: Collapsing Stars
effect: Pulls foes toward caster with gravity projectile volley

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires a great magical comet. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Charging enhances potency. The greatest of the Karolos Conspectus's sorceries, that only a very few sorcerers have ever mastered.
location: Loot: Academy of Raya Lucaria Found on a corpse behind an Illusory Wall near the entrance to the Debate Parlor.
whatItIs: Casting it hurls a great comet at whatever it is aimed at. It costs 24 FP and demands 52 Intelligence, and it can be fired while moving or back to back.
whyItMatters: The comet hits hard in a single shot, so it is a clean answer to a lone big target or a boss that stands still. A high-Intelligence caster wants it as a go-to single-target tool.
whenToUse: Break the Illusory Wall near the entrance to the Debate Parlor in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, and Comet is on a corpse just behind the wall. Equip it once 52 Intelligence is in reach and use it as a single-target finisher.
name: Comet
effect: Fires a great magic comet

desc: Legendary sorcery devised by Azur, primeval sorcerer. Fires a tremendous comet in a torrent akin to the distant starry expanse, the place said to be the origin of glintstone. Hold to continue releasing the sorcery's power. When Azur glimpsed into the primeval current, he saw darkness. He was left both bewitched and fearful of the abyss.
location: Quest Item: Hermit Village Comet Azur is obtained by interacting with Primeval Sorcerer Azur, found on the cliffs southeast of the Hermit Village in Mt. Gelmir.
whatItIs: It launches a tremendous comet wrapped in a torrent of stars. It costs 40 FP across 3 slots and needs 60 Intelligence, and holding it keeps the comet releasing its power.
whyItMatters: It hits like a meteor and keeps going while the button is held, so it is built for overwhelming a single huge target. A max-Intelligence caster will keep it as a heavy single-target tool.
whenToUse: Talk to Primeval Sorcerer Azur, found on the cliffs southeast of the Hermit Village in Mt. Gelmir, and interact to receive it. It is a heavy single-target cast best reserved for bosses and other big, slow targets.
name: Comet Azur
effect: Fires a tremendous comet within a starry torrent

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires a volley of glintstone crystal shards. Charging increases potency. A sorcery of the Crystal Cadre, a group of sorcerers who pursue the wisdom of stone — the secrets locked in the faint cogitation of the Crystalians.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold Sold for 1,500 Runes by Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins. Should Sellen die before purchasing this Sorcery from her, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden...
whatItIs: A sorcery of the Crystal Cadre that looses a volley of glintstone crystal shards. It costs 14 FP and wants 23 Intelligence, and the charge boosts the damage.
whyItMatters: The spread of shards hits a wider area than a single bolt, so it is a good pick for taking down groups at range. A caster who needs a low-cost crowd answer will find it forgiving.
whenToUse: Buy it for 1,500 Runes from Sorceress Sellen, who sells it in Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, the Academy of Raya Lucaria, or Roundtable Hold, or from the Twin Maiden Husks if she is gone. It is an early caster tool for handling small groups.
name: Crystal Barrage
effect: Fires a volley of glintstone crystal shards

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires a burst of glintstone crystal shards. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Charging increases potency. A sorcery of the Crystal Cadre, a group of sorcerers who pursued the wisdom of stone — the secrets locked in the faint cogitation of the Crystalians.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Weeping Peninsula Acquired from defeating the Demi-Human Queen of the Demi-Human Forest Ruins.
whatItIs: Firing it sends a tight burst of glintstone crystal shards at the target. It costs 14 FP and needs 18 Intelligence, and it can be cast repeatedly and while moving.
whyItMatters: The low Intelligence gate and the fast repeat cast make it one of the first solid caster tools a build can pick up. It is a good early answer for single foes and for chipping at small groups.
whenToUse: Defeat the Demi-Human Queen of the Demi-Human Forest Ruins in the Weeping Peninsula, and it is a guaranteed drop. Equip it on a young Intelligence build and use it as a quick, cheap hit while stronger sorceries are still out of reach.
name: Crystal Burst
effect: Fires a burst of glintstone crystal shards

desc: Sorcery of the mysterious Crystalians. Creates a mass of crystal, then shatters it to scour a wide area with a violent rain of crystal shards. This sorcery is used by high-ranking adepts among the Crystalians. Some also call this sorcery "the Crystal Sun."
location: Guaranteed Drop: Academy Crystal Cave Acquired from defeating the Crystalian duo guarding the end of the Cave.
whatItIs: Firing it raises a mass of crystal that then shatters into a wide rain of shards. It costs 34 FP and wants 41 Intelligence, and the charge makes the burst heavier.
whyItMatters: The wide area of effect makes it a strong pick for clearing groups and for catching a boss that keeps strafing. A mid-Intelligence caster will value it as a zone-clearing answer.
whenToUse: Defeat the Crystalian duo guarding the end of the Academy Crystal Cave, and it drops. It is a good mid-point tool for a caster who needs to hit a spread-out group at once.
name: Crystal Release
effect: Scours area with violent rain of crystal shards

desc: Sorcery of the mysterious Crystalians. Creates a mass of crystal, then fires off shards in rapid succession. Hold to continue firing shards. The wrath of the Crystalians encapsulated in sorcery. Each shard is of substantial size, making even a stray blow capable of inflicting a severe wound.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Caelid Acquired from defeating the Putrid Crystalians at the bottom of the Sellia Hideaway.
whatItIs: Casting it creates a mass of crystal and then fires shards in rapid succession. It costs 34 FP and needs 47 Intelligence, and holding it keeps the shards coming.
whyItMatters: The sustained spray of large shards is good for pinning a single target or for chewing through a cluster. A caster with 47 Intelligence will find it a dependable area tool.
whenToUse: Defeat the Putrid Crystalians at the bottom of the Sellia Hideaway in Caelid, and it is the drop. It fits a caster who wants a held, area-hitting answer for mid and late fights.
name: Crystal Torrent
effect: Scours area with violent rain of crystal shards

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Alleviates poison buildup and cures poison. This incantation can be cast while in motion. The Two Fingers has high hopes for the Tarnished; that even if they should be wounded, even should they fall, they will continue to fight for their duty.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Cure Poison is sold for 800 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price,...
whatItIs: It removes poison buildup and cures poison on the caster. It costs 7 FP and asks for 10 Faith, and it can be cast while moving.
whyItMatters: Poison is a common ailment in the Lands Between, and having a dedicated cure stops a slow drip from becoming a death. A Faith build or a caster running low on a heal will want it in the rotation.
whenToUse: Cast it the instant the poison status starts draining health, or ahead of a fight against enemies that apply the buildup effect. It earns a slot from the first region onward because poison enemies show up everywhere. Brother Corhyn carries it at Roundtable Hold, at Altus Plateau, at Leyndell, Royal Capital, and at the Mountaintops of the Giants, or the Twin Maiden Husks handle it after he is gone.
name: Cure Poison
effect: Alleviates poison buildup and cures poison

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' servants, who once served as the assassins of the Roundtable Hold. Creates a veil of darkness that conceals the caster. This incantation can be cast while in motion or crouching. The assassins were themselves once Tarnished who had strayed from guidance, and they pursued their duty in the darkness that is without grace.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 3,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Assassin's Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and that...
whatItIs: A Two Fingers incantation that shrouds the caster in concealment, hiding them from enemy sight. It asks for a moderate Faith investment and a middling FP cost, and it can be cast mid-stride or while crouched.
whyItMatters: Stealth is rare in this game, and the concealment lets the caster back out of a bad fight or slip past a patrol. A Faith build that wants a way to disengage or sneak will find it useful.
whenToUse: Give the Assassin's Prayerbook to Brother Corhyn or to Miriel, Pastor of Vows, and one of them sells it for 3,500 Runes from Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or Mountaintops of the Giants. Use it to disengage from a fight or to slip past enemies that would otherwise engage.
name: Darkness
effect: Creates area of darkness that conceals caster

desc: Incantation that channels the power of the ancient dragon Fortissax, now corrupted by Death. Strikes surroundings with a storm of Death lightning. Inflicts Death blight upon foes. Charging extends duration of the storm. It is said that this golden lightning was wielded by Godwyn, who befriended Fortissax.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Casting it strikes the surroundings with a storm of Death lightning and inflicts Death blight on foes. It costs 28 FP across 2 slots and wants 47 Faith, and the charge extends the storm.
whyItMatters: Death blight is a damage type that ignores much of a target's normal resistances, so it shines against enemies that shrug off other elements. A high-Faith caster will keep it for bosses and other tough single targets.
whenToUse: Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia, or duplicate it in a Wandering Mausoleum. It is a heavy single-target cast to reserve for the hardest fights.
name: Death Lightning
effect: Strikes surroundings with storm of death lightning

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. Produces a ring of light and fires it forwards. The ring of light returns to a position close to the caster before disappearing. This incantation can be cast repeatedly. A gift from the young Miquella to his father, Radagon.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 11,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Goldmask's location in Altus. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation after moving to Goldmask's location, then the player can...
whatItIs: Firing it sends a ring of light forward that then returns close to the caster before fading. It costs 3 FP and needs 13 Intelligence and 13 Faith, and it can be cast repeatedly.
whyItMatters: The tiny FP cost and the returning ring make it a low-commitment poke for chipping foes or testing range. A mixed Intelligence-and-Faith build will like it as a cheap, safe answer.
whenToUse: Buy it for 11,000 Runes from Brother Corhyn after he moves to Goldmask's location in Altus, or from the Twin Maiden Husks if he is gone by then. It is a later-Faith tool that stays useful as a low-cost hit.
name: Discus of Light
effect: Fires ring of light before the caster

desc: The tempest of the Dancing Lion, wielded as an incantation. A whirlwind-like twist of the body summons a storm, launching a tornado forward. Charging enhances potency. The majority of divine beasts were gored and hung upon Messmer's spears, then burned in his flame. Those who witnessed the deed likened it to a funeral pyre for the tower itself.
location: Loot: Ancient Ruins of Rauh Drops from the Divine Beast Dancing Lion found by heading east-northeast across the bridge beginning at the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace. The temple's location is just northeast of the Temple Town Ruins Site of Grace but isn't reachable from that spot.
whatItIs: Summoning a storm is the effect, and it launches a tornado forward. It costs 24 FP and wants 28 Faith, and the charge makes the tornado hit harder.
whyItMatters: The tornado hits a broad line and can knock foes off balance, so it is a good pick for opening a fight or for resetting a boss. A Faith build that wants a big, sweeping hit will find it satisfying.
whenToUse: Divine Beast Tornado belongs to the Shadow of the Erdtree add-on. The Divine Beast Dancing Lion drops it, and the fight sits east-northeast across the bridge that starts at the Ancient Ruins, Grand Stairway Site of Grace, near the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Slot it in as an opener on a Faith build to knock large targets off their feet.
name: Divine Beast Tornado
effect: Summons a storm that launches a tornado forward

desc: A technique of the divine bird warriors, the very first of all horned warriors, wielded as an incantation. Spread the arms wide like wings to release a flurry of feathers. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Hold to continue releasing feathers. The divine bird warriors, and indeed this technique, are said to bear resemblance to the golden Crucible.
location: Divine Bird Feathers is looted from a body at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. It is found in a body of water just east of the Church of the Bud, Main Entrance site of grace. To reach it, head north from the grace and keep to the right in the temple to arrive at the pool, where it's on a body just...
whatItIs: An incantation that spreads the arms wide like wings and releases a flurry of feathers. It costs 3 FP and wants 24 Faith, and holding it keeps the feathers coming.
whyItMatters: The low FP cost and the sustained spray make it a cheap, safe poke for chipping foes or for covering a reposition. A Faith build that wants a low-cost ranged hit will find it reliable.
whenToUse: Available only through the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. A corpse resting in the pool at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh holds it, reached by heading north from the Church of the Bud, Main Entrance site of grace and keeping right inside the temple. It is a cheap FP nudge that works well as a crowd-control filler on a Faith build.
name: Divine Bird Feathers
effect: Spreads arms like wings and releases a flurry of feathers

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Increases holy damage negation. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Follow the path that has been set for you, and you will make enemies of all others: the monks, the sorcerers, the ancient dragon knights, and the scions of gold. Heed me — the Lands Between offers no welcome to the Tarnished.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Weeping Peninsula Divine Fortification is obtained upon defeating the Teardrop Scarab found atop a fallen ruin near the Tombsward Ruins.
whatItIs: Divine Fortification is a Two Fingers incantation that hardens the character against holy attacks for a stretch of time. The Faith requirement sits low, the FP cost is small, and it works while moving.
whyItMatters: The holy resistance buff is a cheap way to shrug off holy attacks, which a number of bosses and elite foes rely on. A Faith build facing holy-heavy fights will want it slotted in.
whenToUse: The Teardrop Scarab perched on a fallen ruin near the Tombsward Ruins in the Weeping Peninsula drops it on defeat, no luck involved. Pop it before any encounter where the enemy leans on holy strikes, and the extra negation keeps your HP bar from dipping as fast.
name: Divine Fortification
effect: Increases holy damage negation

desc: Superior incantation of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons lightning to bolster the caster's body. Attacks become easier to deflect and resistance to all ailments is increased. However, lightning damage negation will be reduced. Only those loved by dragons can survive the ordeal of cladding their bodies in lightning.
location: Loot: Altus Plateau Dragonbolt Blessing is found in a treasure chest within Stormcaller Church.
whatItIs: Channeling it wraps the caster in lightning that makes attacks easier to deflect and raises resistance to ailments. It costs 20 FP and wants 21 Faith, and the trade-off is reduced lightning damage negation.
whyItMatters: The deflect bonus is the real prize, because it makes parrying and riposting more forgiving. A Faith build that leans on a shield or a parry will find it a solid defensive buff.
whenToUse: Open the treasure chest within Stormcaller Church on the Altus Plateau, and it is inside. Equip it before fights where deflecting or riposting is the plan.
name: Dragonbolt Blessing
effect: Bolsters caster's body with lightning

desc: Special incantation of the ancient dragon Florissax. Calls down red lightning to bolster the caster and nearby allies.
