While enrobed with red lightning, all forms of damage negation (including physical) are increased. This also increases damage negation while guarding as an additional effect. There was a time when the priestess never knew love, and thus never used this incantation herself.
location: Quest Item: Jagged Peak Given by the Dragon Communion Priestess at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion after giving her Thiollier's Concoction at night and waiting for her to wake up (and then repeatedly talking to her), and then finally defeating Bayle the Dread.
whatItIs: Channeling it calls down red lightning that bolsters the caster and nearby allies. It costs 35 FP and wants 52 Faith, and while active it raises all forms of damage negation, including physical, plus a bonus while guarding.
whyItMatters: The broad damage-negation buff makes the caster and allies much harder to kill, which is a big deal in any tough fight. A high-Faith build will value it as a defensive anchor.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is required for Dragonbolt of Florissax. On Jagged Peak, hand Thiollier's Concoction to the Dragon Communion Priestess at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion at night, let her wake, chat with her a few times, then fall Bayle the Dread to claim it. Cast it before tough fights to blanket yourself and any nearby allies in reduced damage taken.
name: Dragonbolt of Florissax
effect: Calls down red lightning to bolster self and nearby allies

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to tear through foes with dragon claws. Allows one follow-up attack. Incantation of those who have hunted dragons and feasted upon their hearts. Theirs is a pure and overwhelming power.
location: Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion in the Realm of Shadow for 1 Dragon Heart.
whatItIs: Summoning a dragon lets it rend foes with claws, with one follow-up attack allowed. It costs 24 FP and wants 17 Faith and 13 Arcane.
whyItMatters: The dragon transformation lets the caster trade blows up close, which is unusual for an incantation. A Faith-and-Arcane build that wants a melee-style incantation will find it handy.
whenToUse: Acquire it from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion in the Realm of Shadow, each for 1 Dragon Heart. Use it in close quarters where a normal spell would whiff.
name: Dragonclaw
effect: Channels dragon to rend foes with dragon claws

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew flaming breath. Charging extends duration. Incantation of those who have hunted dragons and feasted upon their hearts. Theirs is a pure and overwhelming power.
location: Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.
whatItIs: Summoning a dragon lets it spew flaming breath at the target. It costs 28 FP and wants 15 Faith and 12 Arcane, and holding it extends the breath.
whyItMatters: The sustained flame breath pins a foe in place and softens a large target before a finishing blow, making it a reliable tool in close quarters. A build that pairs Faith with Arcane and craves a held, area-denying incantation will slot this in early.
whenToUse: Spit the charged flame into a staggering dragon or a sprawling beast in open terrain, then follow up with a heavy strike before it recovers. It suits a Faith-leaning caster and earns its keep from the opening chapters. Buy it with a single Dragon Heart from the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, or from the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or from the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak.
name: Dragonfire
effect: Channels dragon to spew flame breath

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew icy breath. Charging extends duration. Those extraordinary individuals who perpetuate Dragon Communion are called the dragon-hearted.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart.
whatItIs: The caster becomes a dragon and breathes a wide cone of frost that chills everything in its path. It costs 36 FP and asks for 15 Faith and 12 Arcane. Holding the cast button before release extends how long the breath lasts.
whyItMatters: The wide cone builds frost on everyone it touches, and a broken frost proc leaves enemies dealing less damage and recovering stamina slower for a few seconds. The dragon-heart price to buy it is a small barrier early on but the safety it provides is worth the detour. A caster who wants to weaken enemies at range rather than trade hits will find it a steady workhorse.
whenToUse: Pull it out whenever a group of enemies swarms at once or when a boss is in its close-range attack phase and needs to be pushed back. It is acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart, so grab it once that area opens up. Holding the button longer is the right call against a tough target that can survive a quick tap.
name: Dragonice
effect: Channels dragon to spew icy breath

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to bite enemies before them. Incantation of those who have hunted dragons and feasted upon their hearts. Theirs is a pure and overwhelming power.
location: Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion in the Realm of Shadow for 1 Dragon Heart.
whatItIs: A dragon lunges forward in a biting strike right in front of the caster, hitting whatever is directly ahead. It costs 34 FP and needs 24 Faith and 16 Arcane. It charges like other dragon incantations, extending the bite's reach and power.
whyItMatters: The bite is a focused burst that hits a single target squarely, making it precise against one large enemy where a cone spell would waste damage on the air around it. A caster who wants to close the gap and land a clean hit will find it more reliable than a breath in tight corridors. It asks for more Faith than Dragonice, so a mid-game Faith build is the natural fit.
whenToUse: Cast it when a single enemy is lined up in front and a direct hit matters more than area coverage. It can be acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion in the Realm of Shadow for 1 Dragon Heart. Charging before release is worth the extra FP against a boss with a clear front-facing weak spot.
name: Dragonmaw
effect: Channels dragon to bite foes before caster

desc: Superior incantation of Dragon Communion. Channels the power of Ekzykes, the Decaying. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew scarlet rot breath from above. Charging extends duration. This incantation can be cast while jumping. Ekzykes, Dragon Communion Revenger, did not forget his hatred even as he succumbed to the scarlet rot.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Decaying Ekzykes in Caelid.
whatItIs: Scarlet rot breath rains down from above as the caster takes on a dragon form, coating the ground below in a toxic burst. It costs 48 FP and asks for 23 Faith and 15 Arcane. The cast can be released mid-jump, and holding the button extends the breath's duration.
whyItMatters: Scarlet rot ignores armor and deals damage over time, so it punishes heavy-armored enemies that shrug off physical hits. The mid-air cast opens up approaches that a ground-based breath cannot match, letting a caster strike a boss while dodging its attack. The gate of defeating Decaying Ekzykes first means it rewards a Caelid boss fight that most builds will do anyway.
whenToUse: Cast it mid-jump to blanket a large boss with scarlet rot from above, or when an armored foe shrugs off most physical hits and needs a corrosion burst instead. Once Decaying Ekzykes has fallen in Caelid, the altar inside the Cathedral of Dragon Communion will trade it for Dragon Hearts. Holding the cast longer stretches the breath arc wider, which helps cover a boss that shifts position during the attack.
name: Ekzykes's Decay
effect: Spews scarlet rot breath of Ekzykes from above

desc: This legendary incantation is the most ancient of those that derive from the Erdtree. Creates a stream of golden shooting stars that assail the area. It is said that long ago, the Greater Will sent a golden star bearing a beast into the Lands Between, which would later become the Elden Ring.
location: Loot: Deeproot Depths Elden Stars can be looted from a body at the end of a cave filled with giant ants in the Deeproot Depths, located immediately west of the Great Waterfall Crest grace, after climbing up one of the large roots.
whatItIs: Golden shooting stars arc across a wide area in a continuous stream, each one dealing damage to whatever it touches. It costs 41 FP and needs 50 Faith. There is no charge mechanic; every cast delivers the same effect.
whyItMatters: The stars hit a broad zone and do not care about the evasion a melee attacker would use, making it a strong answer to enemies that keep resetting their position. The 50 Faith gate means it is a late-game commitment that rewards a dedicated incantation caster. A pure Faith build that has pushed its stats into the upper range will find it a satisfying endgame tool.
whenToUse: Cast it when multiple enemies are spread out in an open arena or when a boss has a long recovery animation and cannot dodge the stream. It is looted from a body at the end of a cave filled with giant ants in the Deeproot Depths, located immediately west of the Great Waterfall Crest grace, after climbing up one of the large roots. The high Faith requirement means it is a reward for a build that has committed to the incantation path early.
name: Elden Stars
effect: Creates a stream of golden shooting stars that assail the area

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Enchants armament held in the right hand with lightning-affinity attacks.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 4,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then...
whatItIs: The armament in the right hand gains lightning affinity for as long as the buff persists. It costs 21 FP and needs 15 Faith. It is a pure buff with no projectile and no direct damage to an enemy.
whyItMatters: Lightning damage is effective against enemies that resist other damage types, so swapping the weapon's affinity mid-fight can turn a stalemate into a winning exchange. A mixed Faith-and-physical build can slot it in without giving up its main weapon or its incantation loadout. The low FP cost means keeping it active is cheap enough to maintain through most encounters.
whenToUse: Equip it before a fight against an enemy that is taking reduced damage from the current weapon type, then re-cast it after the buff wears off. It is sold for 4,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook. The 15 Faith requirement is low enough that most Faith and hybrid builds will have it available within the first few hours.
name: Electrify Armament
effect: Enchants right-hand armament with lightning damage

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Calls down lightning to charge the caster's body. While charged, electric shocks will strike the area several times. Charging increases potency. The origin of incantations that bolster the body with lightning, and now a lost art in the Lands Between.
location: Loot: Fog Rift Catacombs Found by dropping down a hole in the second cubicle on the left at the third dropping spike-roof and then taking a left twice to find it in the same rooms as a Catacombs Sorcerer, some Fulgurbloom, and a few Skeletal Slimes.
whatItIs: Lightning strikes the caster's body, then electric shocks ripple outward across the surrounding area in rapid succession. It costs 26 FP and needs 30 Faith. Holding the cast button before release increases the potency of each shock.
whyItMatters: The charged body turns the caster into a hazard to approach, so enemies that rush in to punish a slow incantation caster get shocked in return. It is a defensive-offensive hybrid: the damage to nearby enemies is the trade-off for buying time to recover FP or position. A Faith build with room in its FP pool will find it a versatile tool in both solo and co-op play.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion gates access to Electrocharge. Cast it the instant a melee foe commits to a swing, then sidestep and let the charged shocks cover the space where the enemy was standing. It is hidden deep in the Fog Rift Catacombs, past a dropped-down passage on the second cubicle to the left beyond the third spike-roof, then two lefts into a room shared with a Catacombs Sorcerer, some Fulgurbloom, and a few Skeletal Slimes.
name: Electrocharge
effect: Calls down lightning to charge body with electricity

desc: One of the ancient Erdtree incantations. Heals a vast amount of HP for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. The Erdtree once flourished with abundance—yet it was only for a fleeting moment. Such is the course of all life.
location: Loot: Leyndell, Ashen Capital Erdtree Heal is located near the Queen's Bedchamber Site of Grace in Leyndell after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.
whatItIs: Healing golden light restores a large amount of HP for the caster and any nearby allies standing within range. It costs 65 FP and needs 42 Faith. Holding the cast button delays activation, letting the caster time the heal to a safe moment.
whyItMatters: A single cast can turn a near-death situation back into a comfortable health pool, which is invaluable against bosses that chain multiple attacks in quick succession. The fact that it heals allies too makes it the go-to heal for co-op play where a partner might be in trouble. The 65 FP cost is steep, so it is a commitment for a caster who has the FP pool to spare.
whenToUse: Cast it during a boss's recovery window or when a co-op partner's health bar drops below half. It is located near the Queen's Bedchamber Site of Grace in Leyndell after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. The high FP cost means saving it for genuinely dangerous moments rather than topping off after every minor hit is the sensible approach.
name: Erdtree Heal
effect: Vastly heals HP for self and nearby allies

desc: Forbidden sorcery of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. Creates a space of darkness that draws in sorceries and incantations. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Originally a lost sorcery of the Eternal City; the despair that brought about its ruin made manifest.
location: Loot: Caelid Acquired from a corpse inside the Swamp Lookout Tower, guarded by a Bloodhound Knight.
whatItIs: Darkness pools on the ground and pulls nearby sorceries and incantations toward the caster, neutralizing projectiles that would otherwise hit. It costs 25 FP and needs 35 Intelligence. It can be cast while moving, so it slots into a dodge without breaking momentum.
whyItMatters: Pulling an enemy's spell toward the caster removes a projectile that would otherwise land a hit, which is a defensive tool that no other spell in the game replicates. A caster who keeps getting hit by ranged attacks in the mid to late game will find it a significant quality-of-life improvement. The 35 Intelligence requirement is moderate, so most Intelligence builds will have it equipped by the time they reach Caelid.
whenToUse: Cast the moment an enemy begins to charge a projectile spell, because pulling that spell into the dark void negates it before it can reach you. The sorcery is looted from a corpse inside the Swamp Lookout Tower in Caelid, and the Bloodhound Knight guarding that spot makes the pickup a proper fight. An Intelligence build that has passed the early game will find the stat threshold comfortable by the time Caelid opens up.
name: Eternal Darkness
effect: Creates a dark space that draws in spells

desc: Sorcery of the servants of Death. Strike the ground with the staff, triggering an explosion of ghostflame that burns the surrounding area. In the time when there was no Erdtree, death was burned in ghostflame. Deathbirds were the keepers of that fire.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Consecrated Snowfield Acquired from defeating the Death Rite Bird that roams the northern edge of the frozen river at night.
whatItIs: The staff strikes the ground, detonating a burst of ghostflame that covers a wide radius around the impact point. It costs 36 FP and asks for 42 Intelligence and 30 Faith. The explosion is the entire effect; there is no lingering zone or follow-up.
whyItMatters: The wide area makes it effective against groups of enemies that cluster together, and the ghostflame damage type is distinct from regular fire so some enemies take it differently than a standard flame incantation. A build that mixes Intelligence and Faith can use it alongside other sorceries without conflict. The dual stat requirement places it in the mid-to-late game range for hybrid casters.
whenToUse: Cast it when a cluster of enemies is grouped up in front, or when a boss is in a long cast animation and cannot dodge the explosion. It is acquired from defeating the Death Rite Bird that roams the northern edge of the frozen river at night in the Consecrated Snowfield. The night-only spawn window and the high stat gates make it a reward for thorough exploration of the snowfield.
name: Explosive Ghostflame
effect: Causes ghostflame explosion that burns wide area

desc: Sorcery of Fia, the Deathbed Companion. Creates a deathly mist before the caster, which inflicts Death blight upon those who enter. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Charging enhances range of the mist. This sorcery was developed to oppose the Roundtable Hold, and is effective only against the Tarnished.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Deeproot Depths Acquired from defeating Fia's Champions.
whatItIs: Deathly mist spreads in front of the caster, inflicting Death blight on any enemy that walks through the cloud. It costs 25 FP and needs 23 Intelligence and 18 Faith. Holding the button extends the mist's range, and it can be cast while moving.
whyItMatters: Death blight is a status effect that builds toward an instant kill, so the mist turns a zone into a trap for any enemy that has to cross it. It works only against the Tarnished, which makes it a PVP tool rather than a PVE one, and a mixed Intelligence-and-Faith build can slot it in as a zone-control option without sacrificing damage output. The dual stat requirement is low enough that it is accessible in the mid-game.
whenToUse: Deploy it in a narrow corridor or in front of a doorway before a fight begins, then back away and let enemies walk into the mist on their own. It is acquired from defeating Fia's Champions in the Deeproot Depths. The death blight buildup is slow enough that it works best against enemies that have to cross the mist area to reach a target rather than against a single stationary opponent.
name: Fia's Mist
effect: Release a mist of death before caster

desc: Incantation of the Fire Knights under Messmer the Impaler's personal command. Launch a serpentine flame that bends and curls in pursuit of its foe. Charging enhances potency. When the flame they received from Messmer would not find purchase within them, the Fire Knights relied on fire incantations to honor their bond.
location: Loot: Shadow Keep From the Storehouse, Back Section Site of Grace, head west to find a ladder on a banister and head up it. Head right at the top of the ladder and take the stairs to another floor and continue forwards until you reach a small balcony with a body holding this Incantation.
whatItIs: A curling stream of flame that bends toward its target rather than flying straight, so it tracks enemies that move unpredictably. The incantation draws on Faith and asks for a modest stat investment, while holding the cast button longer before release makes the serpent grow fiercer. It is a Messmerfire rite suited to single-target pressure on foes that dodge a direct bolt.
whyItMatters: The homing behavior means it connects on targets that would dodge a straight-line bolt, making it forgiving for new casters who are still learning enemy movement patterns. The low FP cost and stat requirement make it accessible early in a Faith build. A caster who wants a reliable single-target hit that does not demand perfect aim will find it a steady option in the early and mid portions of the DLC.
whenToUse: Access to the Shadow of the Erdtree content is a prerequisite for finding Fire Serpent. Use it on a single fast-moving enemy where a straight-line projectile would overshoot, letting the serpentine path close the gap. Start at the Storehouse, Back Section Site of Grace in Shadow Keep, walk west to a banister ladder, climb it, turn right at the top, take the stairs up, and follow the corridor until a body rests on a small balcony.
name: Fire Serpent
effect: Launches a flame with a serpentine coil

desc: Incantation originating from a deeply ominous prophecy. Sets both the caster and the surrounding area ablaze with raging flames. The caster's body will remain engulfed in flame for a while, burning them and any who draw near. Charging enhances potency. The prophet despaired, looking up at the Erdtree, for soon the kindling would burst into flame, bringing ruin.
location: Painting Item: Altus Plateau Left behind by the spirit of an artist located near the southern cliffs at the top of Dominula, Windmill Village, south of the Windmill Heights Site of Grace after acquiring "Flightless Bird" Painting.
whatItIs: Raging flames engulf both the caster and the surrounding area, burning the caster as well as any enemy that draws close. It costs 26 FP and needs 19 Faith. The caster remains ablaze for a period after casting, and holding the button increases the intensity.
whyItMatters: The self-burning aspect turns the caster into a walking hazard, which punishes enemies that rush in to close the gap while the caster is committed to a cast. It is a defensive-offensive hybrid where the damage taken is the trade-off for keeping melee attackers at bay. A Faith build that wants an area denial tool without a long cooldown will find it versatile in tight spaces.
whenToUse: Cast it when a melee enemy is lunging in and the caster needs to create space without backpedaling into a wall. It is left behind by the spirit of an artist near the southern cliffs at the top of Dominula, Windmill Village, south of the Windmill Heights Site of Grace in the Altus Plateau, after acquiring the Flightless Bird Painting. The self-damage means it is not a repeat-spam option; save it for moments when the trade-off is worth the HP lost.
name: Fire's Deadly Sin
effect: Sets area and self ablaze with raging flames

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Increases fire damage negation. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Follow the path that has been set for you, and you will make enemies of all others: the monks, the sorcerers, the ancient dragon knights, and the scions of gold. Heed me — the Lands Between offers no welcome to the Tarnished.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 3,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving...
whatItIs: A protective incantation of the Two Fingers that builds up resistance to fire damage for the caster. It draws a modest amount of FP, asks for a low Faith threshold, and remains active even while the character is in motion, so it slots neatly into a dodge or a roll. The effect lasts for a set duration and then fades, requiring a recast if the threat persists.
whyItMatters: Fire damage shows up throughout the game, from enemy attacks to environmental hazards, so a buff that reduces it pays dividends in nearly every zone. The Faith threshold is among the gentlest in the game, which means even a light hybrid build can field it from early on. The modest FP demand means the buff can stay active through long fights without draining the resource pool noticeably.
whenToUse: Cast it before entering an area dense with fire-based enemies or before a boss fight that involves heavy fire attacks. It is sold for 3,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn, available in Roundtable Hold, the Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and the Mountaintops of the Giants. If Brother Corhyn dies before the purchase, the Twin Maiden Husks sell it for the same price after receiving the relevant prayerbook.
name: Flame Fortification
effect: Increases fire damage negation

desc: This legendary incantation is one of several that draws directly from the power of the Fire Giants. Releases a ball of raging fire said to be inhabited by a fell god. The fireball floats toward enemies and explodes, setting the area ablaze. Arghanthy, the chief guardian of the Flame, had kept this incantation a well-kept secret until it was stolen by Adan. The fell god still lurks within the Fire Giants.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Received upon defeating Adan, Thief of Fire, the boss trapped in the Malefactor's Evergaol.
whatItIs: Flame of the Fell God is a Giantsflame incantation that launches a large ball of fire toward the target, which bursts on impact and sets the surrounding ground ablaze. It demands a heavy Faith investment, a large slot footprint, and a substantial FP cost, making it a tool for a dedicated caster. The lingering fire on the ground pressures enemies that try to reposition during a boss fight.
whyItMatters: The fireball homes toward its target, so it connects even on a moving enemy, and the explosion covers a wide area afterward. The 2-slot cost means it competes with two other incantations for space, so it is a deliberate choice for a caster who wants a heavy burst tool. A pure Faith build with the stat to spare will find it a satisfying payoff for the slot investment.
whenToUse: Cast it when a single tough enemy is in an open space and a wide-area explosion is needed to finish the exchange. It is received upon defeating Adan, Thief of Fire, the boss trapped in the Malefactor's Evergaol in Liurnia of the Lakes. The 2-slot cost and the 41 Faith gate both push it into the mid-to-late game for a dedicated incantation build.
name: Flame of the Fell God
effect: Summons raging fireball that explodes and sets the area ablaze

desc: Incantation originating from a sinister prophecy. Throws a ball of raging fire. Charging enhances potency and causes the ball of fire to explode. The flame of ruin is anathema to the Erdtree. But prophets sometimes glimpse it within the faith all the same. Sadly, when this occurs their sole reward is banishment.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 800 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them...
whatItIs: Raging fire in its simplest form: a single thrown ball that arcs toward the target. Holding the cast before release boosts potency and triggers an explosion on impact, adding area damage. It needs only a touch of Faith, making it accessible to a new character early on.
whyItMatters: The low FP cost and minimal stat requirement make it very accessible for a new Faith build, available from the first hour of play. The charged explosion adds area damage for a negligible extra FP cost, making it a solid crowd-control option before higher-cost options are in hand. A caster starting a Faith build can rely on it as the default ranged attack and swap it out once something with more reach or damage turns up.
whenToUse: Equip it from the start and use it as the default ranged attack until a stronger fire incantation is in hand. It costs 800 Runes and can be bought from Brother Corhyn at his various shops, or from the Twin Maiden Husks should he be unavailable, anywhere from Roundtable Hold to the Mountaintops of the Giants. Holding the button before release is the right call against any enemy with more than one hit of health.
name: Flame Sling
effect: Throws ball of raging fire

desc: One of the incantations of the Fire Monks. Creates a fire within that burns away toxins. Alleviates poison and scarlet rot buildup and cures these ailments. This incantation leaves the caster with subtle burns—a reminder that they must fear the flame.
location: Loot: Liurnia of the Lakes Flame, Cleanse Me can be looted from a corpse at the Fire Monk campsite located south of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia.
whatItIs: An internal fire burns away toxins, alleviating both poison and scarlet rot buildup and curing either ailment if it has already triggered. It costs 14 FP and needs 12 Faith. It is a pure purification spell with no offensive component and no lasting buff.
whyItMatters: Poison and scarlet rot are the status ailments that appear most frequently in the Lands Between, and it removes both in a single cast. Any build can carry it without conflict because the stat ask is small and it does not stack against other active buffs. The FP cost is gentle enough that a caster can top up from it between major spells without feeling a meaningful drain.
whenToUse: Cast it the moment a status effect bar appears on the HUD, before the buildup completes and starts dealing damage over time. It is looted from a corpse at the Fire Monk campsite located south of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. Keeping it equipped as a backup cure means the character is never caught without a way to clear a stacking status effect in a long fight.
name: Flame, Cleanse Me
effect: Alleviates buildup of and cures poison and scarlet rot

desc: One of the incantations that draws directly from the power of the Fire Giants. Hurls several balls of fire at once. Charging enhances potency and causes the balls of fire to explode. There is no record of this incantation in common prayerbooks. Only a select few prelates know of its existence.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 10,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Giant's Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and that...
whatItIs: Several balls of fire arc out in a spread pattern, each one striking a different point in the target area. It costs 16 FP and needs 28 Faith. Holding the button increases potency and causes each ball to explode on impact, widening the coverage.
whyItMatters: The wide spread of fireballs covers a broad area in one cast, so each projectile can find a different target without the need to re-aim between shots. When charged, the fireballs detonate on impact and turn the attack into a much wider burst, which is useful against large-bodied bosses where a single bolt would only graze the surface. A mid-game Faith build gains a reliable crowd-clearing tool that slots between the smaller single-target rites and the heavier multi-slot options.
whenToUse: Aim it at open crowds of adds or at the wide body of a large boss where landing a clean hit is difficult, and it fits nicely from the early game onward. Its wide spread makes sloppy aiming far less punishing than a focused beam. Hand the Giant's Prayerbook to either Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows, and it lands in their stock at Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and Mountaintops of the Giants.
name: Flame, Fall Upon Them
effect: Hurls several balls of fire at once

desc: Superior incantation of the Fire Monks. Creates an invigorating fire within that enhances physical and fire-affinity attack power. This incantation does not burn the caster, and so it is considered forbidden by the guardians of the Flame.
location: This incantation can be located on a body behind/on the eastern side of Fort Gael in Caelid. It is guarded by two Flame Chariots.
whatItIs: An internal fire takes hold of the caster, raising both physical and fire-affinity attack power without inflicting any damage in return. The incantation costs a moderate amount of FP and asks for a modest Faith investment. There is no visible projectile or area effect, so it functions purely as a buff that boosts every subsequent hit.
whyItMatters: Boosting both physical and fire damage at once makes it useful for a wide range of builds, not just pure incantation casters. The lack of self-burning distinguishes it from other fire-related buffs and makes it safe to keep active during prolonged fights without worrying about HP drain. A hybrid build that mixes a fire weapon with incantations will find it a consistent damage multiplier that is cheap to maintain.
whenToUse: Cast it before a long boss exchange where sustained damage output matters, since the buff persists for a set window and every hit inside that window benefits. The incantation is carried by a corpse on the eastern side of Fort Gael in Caelid, and two Flame Chariots stand guard over the spot. A Faith build that has reached the Caelid stage will typically have the required stat headroom already, so the pickup is straightforward.
name: Flame, Grant Me Strength
effect: Raises physical and fire-affinity attack power

desc: The most ancient of the Fire Monks' incantations. Creates a fire within that greatly increases fire damage negation. It is said that this incantation was used during the War against the Giants long ago, during which it protected the champions of the Erdtree.
location: Loot: Mountaintops of the Giants Flame, Protect Me can be found in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is located behind an imp statue fog wall right next to the dungeon's grace. One Stonesword Key is required to access it.
whatItIs: Fire resistance increases substantially as an internal fire takes hold, greatly reducing the damage the caster takes from fire-based attacks. It costs 30 FP and needs 24 Faith. It is a pure defensive buff with no offensive component and no visible flame on the character.
whyItMatters: Fire damage is one of the most common sources of damage in Elden Ring, so a strong resistance buff reduces the threat of many encounters at once without any active management. The 24 Faith requirement is moderate, placing it in the mid-game range for a dedicated incantation build. A caster who regularly faces fire-based enemies or bosses with heavy flame attacks will find it a reliable defensive layer that is cheap enough to keep refreshed.
whenToUse: Equip it ahead of a boss that leans heavily on fire-based attacks, or before pushing through a zone where environmental flames are everywhere. The incantation sits in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave in the Mountaintops of the Giants, tucked behind an imp statue fog wall right next to the dungeon's grace. A Stonesword Key is needed to open the door, so the detour is deliberate and worth planning around for a build that wants extra fire resistance.
name: Flame, Protect Me
effect: Greatly increases fire damage negation

desc: A finger sorcery of Count Ymir, High Priest. One of the secret hallowed rites. Conjures an image of a microcosm at a foe's feet that pulses with a single wave before disappearing in a burst. Charging enhances potency. The broken and discarded are fully willing to cling to fleeting simulacra, earning them some modicum of sympathy.
location: Purchased: Cathedral of Manus Metyr Fleeting Microcosm may be purchased from Count Ymir for 20,000 Runes after ringing the bell at the Finger Ruins of Dheo. He sits on the throne in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr on the Scadu Altus, located in the Realm of Shadow.
whatItIs: An image of a microcosm appears at a foe's feet, pulses with a single wave of energy, then vanishes in a burst. It costs 26 FP and needs 42 Intelligence. Holding the button before release increases the potency of the pulse.
whyItMatters: The single pulse is a focused burst that hits whatever is at the target's feet, making it precise against a single enemy without wasting damage on the surrounding air. The 42 Intelligence requirement places it firmly in the late-game range for a dedicated sorcery build. It is a niche tool: effective when a clean, precise hit matters, less useful against a group of spread-out enemies that a cone or spread spell would handle better.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be installed before Fleeting Microcosm can be obtained. Use it on a stationary or slow-moving target where a clean single-hit is preferable to a wide splash, since the microcosm focuses its pulse into a concentrated burst. Count Ymir sells it after the bell at the Finger Ruins of Dheo has been rung; he is seated on the throne in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr on the Scadu Altus in the Realm of Shadow.
name: Fleeting Microcosm
effect: Conjures a microcosm that pulses with a single wave, disappearing in a burst

desc: Incantation that channels the power of the ancient dragon Fortissax. Creates two spears of red lightning and stabs them into the ground from above, one after another. On impact, each spear will burst into trails of lightning covering the area. During the War of the Ancient Dragons, these twin red lightning stakes were the hallmark of one ancient dragon who was called the mightiest boulderstone.
location: Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: Channels the power of the ancient dragon Fortissax to send two red lightning spears slamming down from above in quick succession. Each spear bursts into spreading trails of lightning on impact, covering a wide area. It is a dragon cult incantation demanding 46 Faith and costing 64 FP.
whyItMatters: The wide area of effect makes it effective against groups of enemies and against large bosses that occupy a lot of space. A high-Faith build that has already invested heavily will find the damage output satisfying for the FP spent.
whenToUse: Equip it once Faith is high enough to make the cost feel reasonable, typically in the later stages of the base game. Get it by trading the Remembrance of the Lichdragon to Finger Reader Enia after defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, or by duplicating it in a Wandering Mausoleum; only one copy is obtainable per playthrough through either method.
name: Fortissax's Lightning Spear
effect: Stabs from above with two red lightning spears in tandem

desc: The eldest primeval sorcery, said to have been discovered by an ancient astrologer. A sorcery of legendary status. Summons a dark cloud of stars overhead. Shortly after, the cloud will release a violent deluge of star rain. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Charging increases potency. Thought to be the founding glintstone sorcery. The glimpse of the primeval current that the astrologer saw became real, and the stars' amber rained down on this land.
location: Loot: Heretical Rise, Mountaintops of the Giants You'll need to walk over an invisible bridge across the valley directly east of the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace.
whatItIs: Summons a dark cloud of stars overhead that releases a violent downpour of star rain over a wide area after a short delay. It is a Primeval sorcery requiring 52 Intelligence, costs 27 FP, and can be charged for increased potency.
whyItMatters: The delayed overhead area of effect is useful against crowds of enemies and against bosses that stand still for extended periods. A high-Intelligence caster with room in the FP budget gets reliable damage without needing to track a single target.
whenToUse: Best used in open areas where the star rain has room to spread and where no tall structures block the effect. Loot it in Heretical Rise on Mountaintops of the Giants by walking across the invisible bridge across the valley directly east of the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace.
name: Founding Rain of Stars
effect: Releases a downpour of star rain for a while

desc: Sorcery said to have been used by the old snow witch. Releases a cold mist before the caster. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Charging enhances range of the mist. The snowy crone taught the young Ranni to fear the dark moon as she imparted her cold sorcery.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 6,000 Runes by Preceptor Seluvis. Should Seluvis die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Seluvis's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: Projects a cold mist forward from the caster that slows and damages anything caught in it. It is a Cold sorcery needing only 21 Intelligence, costs 20 FP, and charges to extend the mist range.
whyItMatters: The slow effect buys time to reposition or line up a stronger attack while the enemy struggles to close distance. A low-Intelligence build can still get a solid utility tool from it early on.
whenToUse: Cast it when a fast enemy is closing in or when a boss is lunging, then follow up with a heavier spell while the target is slowed. Purchase it for 6,000 Runes from Preceptor Seluvis in Liurnia of the Lakes or at Roundtable Hold, or buy it from the Twin Maiden Husks using Seluvis's Bell Bearing if he dies first.
name: Freezing Mist
effect: Releases cold mist before caster

desc: Incantation originating from the maddening Three Fingers. Releases concentrated blasts of the yellow flame of frenzy from the caster's eyes. Charging enhances potency, enabling the blasts to penetrate the enemy's guard. In times past, every single person who attempted to control the flame of frenzy succumbed to madness after a desperate internal struggle. This incantation is testament to a meager victory.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Frenzied Burst drops from a Scarab guarded by Frenzied Rats in the middle of a small forest, directly south of the Church of Inhibition in Liurnia.
whatItIs: Emits a concentrated blast of yellow frenzy flame from the caster's eyes in a short, piercing burst. It is a frenzy incantation requiring 22 Faith, costs 24 FP, and charges to gain the ability to break through an enemy's guard.
whyItMatters: The guard-breaking property on a charged cast makes it useful against enemies that block or guard heavily. A Faith build that needs a quick, low-commitment attack can slot it in without worrying about a long recovery.
whenToUse: Use it when an enemy is locked into a guard or shield stance and a normal hit would be blocked. It drops from a Scarab guarded by Frenzied Rats in a small forest directly south of the Church of Inhibition in Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Frenzied Burst
effect: Emits concentrated blast of yellow flame of frenzy from eyes

desc: Sorcery said to have been used by the old snow witch. Enchants armament held in the right hand with frost. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. The snowy crone taught the young Ranni to fear the dark moon as she imparted her cold sorcery.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from felling a Scarab on the road northwest of the Behind Caria Manor Site of Grace.
whatItIs: Enchants the weapon held in the right hand with frost, adding cold damage to every hit for a period. It is a Cold sorcery needing only 15 Intelligence, costs 20 FP, and does not need to be charged.
whyItMatters: It lets a melee or hybrid build bolt on frost damage without switching to a dedicated magic weapon. The low stat requirement means almost any build that can equip a spellbook can use it.
whenToUse: Activate it before engaging a boss or a tough enemy to layer cold buildup on top of physical damage. Acquire it from a Scarab on the road northwest of the Behind Caria Manor Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes.
name: Frozen Armament
effect: Enchants right-hand armament with frost

desc: Incantation that channels the power of the Dragonkin Soldiers. Creates a spear of ice lightning and stabs it into the ground from above. On impact, the spear will burst into trails of lightning advancing forwards. The Dragonkin were born in the Eternal City, where they knew no true sky, nor true lightning. Instead, ice lightning was their weapon.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Ainsel River Frozen Lightning Spear is acquired after defeating the Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella.
whatItIs: Calls down a single ice lightning spear from above that stabs into the ground and bursts into forward-advancing trails of frost lightning. It is a dragon cult incantation requiring 34 Faith and costing 29 FP.
whyItMatters: The forward-advancing lightning trails make it effective against enemies standing in a line or approaching from the front. A mid-Faith build gets a reliable single-target burst without the high cost of the red lightning alternatives.
whenToUse: Cast it when an enemy or boss is directly ahead and standing in open ground where the lightning trails can travel. It is a guaranteed drop after defeating the Dragonkin Soldier of Nokstella in Ainsel River.
name: Frozen Lightning Spear
effect: Stabs with ice lightning spear from above

desc: Incantation of Ansbach, Pureblood Knight. Produces a bloodflame blade from the side of the hand, then lunges at enemies to cleave through them. Charge to increase the number of slashes. Markedly different from the finessed swordplay of the dynast, this is an aggressive last resort of an incantation that gave rise to Ansbach's fearsome reputation.
location: Loot: Enir-Ilim Complete Sir Ansbach's questline while siding with him against Needle Knight Leda and defeat Promised Consort Radahn and then this Incantation (as well as Ansbach's Set and the Obsidian Lamina) can be found on his body, just to the right after entering the boss arena again.
whatItIs: Produces a bloodflame blade from the side of the hand and lunges forward to cleave through enemies in a melee arc. It is a blood incantation requiring 19 Faith and 27 Arcane, costs 18 FP, and charges to increase the number of slashes.
whyItMatters: The close-range slashing makes it useful in tight spaces where a projectile spell would overshoot. A Faith-Arcane hybrid build gets an aggressive option that pairs well with rushing attacks.
whenToUse: Swing it when an enemy is close enough to be hit by the lunge but far enough that a weapon swing would miss. It is found on Sir Ansbach's body in Enir-Ilim after completing his questline against Needle Knight Leda and defeating Promised Consort Radahn; this requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
name: Furious Blade of Ansbach
effect: Cleaves through enemies with bloodflame blade summoned from side of the hand

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Creates a magical greathammer and slams it down. Allows one follow-up attack. Drawn from the scholarly conspectus of Haima, the adjudicator of the academy, this sorcery employs might as a means to quell conflict.
location: Converted Fringe Tower, north-east Liurnia of the Lakes, not to be mistaken with the Converted Tower in the south-west. You will need to use the Erudition gesture given by Thops in front of the statue of Marika. This will reveal a hidden ladder to the top of the tower with a treasure chest that...
whatItIs: Conjures a magical greathammer that slams down before the caster, allowing one follow-up attack. It is a Glintstone sorcery requiring 25 Intelligence, costs 22 FP, and does not require charging.
whyItMatters: The two-hit sequence provides a quick burst of damage at close to medium range without needing to track a target. A mid-Intelligence caster gets a satisfying feel and reliable hit registration.
whenToUse: Use it at medium range against a single enemy or boss that is standing still between attacks. Find it in the Converted Fringe Tower in north-east Liurnia of the Lakes by using the Erudition gesture given by Thops in front of the statue of Marika to reveal a hidden ladder to a treasure chest at the top.
name: Gavel of Haima
effect: Attacks using a magic greathammer

desc: One of the sorceries developed from the magma of Mt. Gelmir. Conjures a surge of magma from the earth, covering the area. Charging extends the surge of magma. This sorcery is held to represent the fury of the volcano, but the arrogance of attempting to harness it is solely that of men and serpents.
location: Quest Item: Volcano Manor Acquired from Knight Bernahl in the Drawing Room of Volcano Manor after successfully defeating Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm with him. This sorcery will be left unobtainable for the rest of the playthrough should Bernahl die before the player joins...
whatItIs: Sends a surge of magma erupting from the ground that covers a wide area in front of the caster. It is a sorcery requiring 28 Intelligence and 15 Faith, costs 27 FP, and charges to extend the magma surge.
whyItMatters: Magma that erupts from the ground covers a wide patch of terrain, so it punishes packs of enemies and bosses that camp in one spot without needing precise aiming. A hybrid build mixing Intelligence and Faith can slot it in without over-investing in either stat, which makes it a flexible pick for caster builds that split points.
whenToUse: Cast it under a boss or a cluster of enemies standing on flat ground where the magma can erupt around them. Acquire it from Knight Bernahl in the Drawing Room of Volcano Manor after defeating Vargram the Raging Wolf and Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm together with him.
name: Gelmir's Fury
effect: Covers area with surge of magma from the earth

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew ghostflame breath. Charging extends duration. The land of spiritgraves is home to all manner of dead, and even the corpses of fallen dragons found their way there. Several of them were endowed with such vivacity that even in death, they could not fully die.
location: Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 3 Dragon Hearts.
whatItIs: Transforms the caster into a dragon that spews a sustained breath of ghostflame forward. It is a dragon incantation requiring 23 Faith and 15 Arcane, costs 36 FP, and charges to extend the duration.
whyItMatters: The sustained breath covers a large forward cone and is effective against crowds and against bosses that charge in from the front. A Faith-Arcane build gets a wide-area tool that does not depend on a single precision hit.
whenToUse: Release it when a cluster of enemies is pushing in from ahead, letting the dragon breath wash over the whole group in one sustained burst. It lives at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak, costing three Dragon Hearts, and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be owned before that altar can be reached.
name: Ghostflame Breath
effect: Channels dragon to spew ghostflame breath

desc: Sorcery of the inquisitors of the tower, wielded as an incantation of the spiral. A swing of the arm releases a giant golden arc. Charging enhances potency. The arc resembles the barb, a known symbol of coercive questioning.
location: Loot: Scadu Altus Found in the Ruins of Unte, within the courtyard blocked by a deactivated Furnace Golem. Reactivate the Furnace Golem with a Hefty Furnace Pot thrown from the top of one of the outer ruins in order to enter the courtyard. The incantation can be found in a chest within the...
whatItIs: Releases a giant golden arc in a sweeping swing of the arm that hits everything in its path. It is an incantation requiring 34 Faith, costs 24 FP, and charges to enhance potency.
whyItMatters: The wide sweeping arc makes it effective against groups of enemies clustered together or against a boss at medium range. A high-Faith build gets a reliable area hit that does not require aiming at a single point.
whenToUse: Sweep it across a tight cluster of foes or across a boss standing beyond melee range, then charge it for a heavier arc that hits harder. It sits in a chest inside the Ruins of Unte in Scadu Altus, reachable by reactivating the Furnace Golem that blocks the courtyard with a Hefty Furnace Pot thrown from the top of an outer ruin, and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is needed to reach that region.
name: Giant Golden Arc
effect: Releases a giant golden arc with a swing of the arm

desc: One of the incantations that draws directly from the power of the Fire Giants. Hurls a massive ball of raging fire. Charging enhances potency and causes the ball of fire to explode. There is no record of this incantation in common prayerbooks. Only a select few prelates know of its existence.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 13,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Giant's Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and that...
whatItIs: Hurls a massive ball of raging fire that travels forward and, when charged, explodes on impact. It is a Giantsflame incantation requiring 30 Faith, costs 30 FP, takes 2 spell slots, and charges to trigger the explosion.
whyItMatters: The explosion on a charged cast makes it a strong single-target burst for bosses and large enemies. The two-slot cost means it competes with other incantations for space in the spellbook.
whenToUse: Charge and throw it at a boss during a recovery window or when the enemy is stationary after a heavy attack. Buy it for 13,000 Runes from Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Giant's Prayerbook; they sell it in Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or Mountaintops of the Giants.
name: Giantsflame Take Thee
effect: Hurls a massive ball of raging fire

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Creates a defensive arch of magic glintblades overhead, which automatically attack nearby foes. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Bestowed upon the enchanted Carian knights, who combined this art with their swordsmanship to maintain pressure upon their foes, striking in waves of steel and sorcery.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold Sold for 2,500 Runes by Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Preceptor Seluvis after giving either of them the Royal House Scroll. Should the scroll be given to one of them and then have that instructor...
whatItIs: Creates a defensive arch of magic glintblades overhead that automatically attacks nearby foes. It is a Carian sorcery requiring 22 Intelligence, costs 18 FP, and can be cast while in motion.
whyItMatters: The automatic attacks mean the caster does not need to aim or track targets while the blades are active. A mid-Intelligence build gets passive area coverage that pairs well with a melee weapon in the other hand.
whenToUse: Activate it before entering a room full of enemies or during a boss fight to add constant chip damage while focusing on movement. Buy it for 2,500 Runes from Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows, or Preceptor Seluvis after giving either of them the Royal House Scroll; they sell it in Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, Academy of Raya Lucaria, or Roundtable Hold.
name: Glintblade Phalanx
effect: Forms a defensive arch of magic glintblades

desc: An old sorcery of the Carian royal family. Creates a sigil overhead, from which three enemy-seeking glintblades appear after a brief delay. This sorcery can be used while in motion. Charging increases the delay. The prototypical form of sword-phalanx sorceries saw a different subsequent refinement in the realm of shadow.
location: Loot: Castle Ensis After progressing through the chapel section, go through the iron gate and fall off a ledge directly to the left. Go around the cliff and climb up the ladders to the rooftop of the chapel. Head northwest and jump down onto a platform, and you will find a corpse that has the spell.
whatItIs: Raises a sigil overhead from which three enemy-seeking glintblades appear after a brief delay. It is a Carian sorcery requiring 28 Intelligence, costs 19 FP, and charges to increase the delay before the blades fire.
whyItMatters: The enemy-seeking nature means the blades home in on targets, reducing the need for precise aim. A mid to high Intelligence build gets a reliable three-hit burst that works against bosses and groups alike.
whenToUse: Let the sigil hang overhead while you sidestep, because the three glintblades launch after a short delay and home in on whatever is in front of them. A corpse in Castle Ensis carries it; work through the chapel section, pass the iron gate, drop off the ledge to the left, climb the ladders up to the rooftop, then head northwest to the platform. The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is what gates access to Castle Ensis entirely.
name: Glintblade Trio
effect: Creates sigil that forms three projectile glintblades after delay

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires a horizontal arc of magic that spreads outward. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Granted to sorcererers who depart from the academy to embark on journeys, in order to fend off large groups of would-be adversaries. Fools often roam in packs.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold One of the starting spells of the Astrologer Origin. x1 Sold for 1,500 Runes by Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins. x1 Sold for 1,500 Runes by Sorcerer Thops at Church of Irith.
whatItIs: Fires a horizontal arc of magic that spreads outward as it travels. It is a Glintstone sorcery requiring only 13 Intelligence, costs 9 FP, and can be cast repeatedly and while in motion.
whyItMatters: The low cost and low stat requirement make it an early-game magic option for a new caster. The spreading arc helps hit multiple enemies at once during early encounters.
whenToUse: Use it as a default ranged attack in the first hours of the game when nothing stronger is available. It is one of the starting spells of the Astrologer Origin, and can be bought for 1,500 Runes from Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins, or from Sorcerer Thops at Church of Irith.
name: Glintstone Arc
effect: Fires a horizontally-widening magic arc

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a dragon to spew magic breath. Charging extends duration. Those extraordinary individuals who perpetuate Dragon Communion are called the dragon-hearted.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart.
whatItIs: A Dragon Communion incantation that changes the caster's form into a dragon and projects a long, sustained cone of magic ahead. It asks for a modest amount of Faith and some Arcane, costs a moderate amount of FP, and holding the charge button stretches how long the breath lasts.
whyItMatters: The sustained forward cone covers a wide area and is effective against groups of enemies charging in from the front. The low stat requirements make it accessible to early Faith or hybrid builds.
whenToUse: Unleash it while a wave of enemies is still closing so the breath catches them mid-advance, or hold it on a boss that stands directly ahead at close range. It is sold from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid in exchange for one Dragon Heart.
name: Glintstone Breath
effect: Channels dragon to spew magic breath.

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires a magical comet with a trailing tail. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Charging enhances potency. A sorcery of the Karolos Conspectus, the most venerable of the academy.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold Sold for 12,000 Runes by Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Preceptor Seluvis after giving either of them the Conspectus Scroll. Should the scroll be given to one of them and then have that instructor...
whatItIs: Sends a magical comet with a trailing tail traveling in a straight line toward the target. It is a Glintstone sorcery requiring 36 Intelligence, costs 17 FP, and charges to enhance potency.
whyItMatters: The straight-line projectile is easy to aim and reliable against single targets at range. A high-Intelligence build gets a satisfying long-range option that does not demand a lot of FP per cast.
whenToUse: When an enemy is winding up a heavy strike or a boss is locked in a combo, let it fly to interrupt the motion, and hold the cast to build a charge that lands with a much heavier hit from range. Hand the Conspectus Scroll to Sorceress Sellen, or to Miriel, Pastor of Vows, or to Preceptor Seluvis, and it appears in their shop across Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, the Academy of Raya Lucaria, and Roundtable Hold.
name: Glintstone Cometshard
effect: Fires a magic comet with a trailing tail

desc: Sorcery said to have been used by the old snow witch. The glintstone serves as a conduit, launching a mass of cold magic. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. The snowy crone taught the young Ranni to fear the dark moon as she imparted her cold sorcery.
location: Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 7,500 Runes by Preceptor Seluvis. Should Seluvis die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Seluvis's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: A Cold sorcery that hurls a chunk of frozen magic straight ahead, hitting for a quick burst of damage on contact. It demands only a modest Intelligence requirement, spends a small amount of FP, and can be fired off in rapid succession while the character is still moving.
whyItMatters: The low cost and simple projectile make it a dependable early-game ranged option. A low-Intelligence build can use it without stretching the FP budget thin.
whenToUse: Slot it in as a low-cost gap filler between heavier castings, or use it to put a finishing hit on a damaged enemy from a safe distance. Preceptor Seluvis sells it in Liurnia of the Lakes, and the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold will also stock it; if Seluvis is gone, hand them Seluvis's Bell Bearing and it appears in their inventory.
name: Glintstone Icecrag
effect: Fires mass of cold magic from glintstone

desc: Glintstone sorcery of Count Ymir, High Priest. One of the finger sorceries said to have been discovered in a hallowed ruin. Flings a magic nail that crumbles during flight. Charging increases potency. Count Ymir boasts that this is mere child's play, an echo of a greater truth.
location: Purchased: Cathedral of Manus Metyr Glintstone Nail may be purchased from Count Ymir for 12,000 Runes after ringing the bell in the Finger Ruins of Rhia.
whatItIs: Flings a magic nail that crumbles during flight, shattering on impact. It is a Finger sorcery of Count Ymir requiring 18 Intelligence, costs 10 FP, and charges to increase potency.
whyItMatters: The low FP cost means it can be spammed in succession without draining the resource bar. A low-Intelligence caster gets a quick, cheap projectile for close to mid-range encounters.
whenToUse: Tap it in quick succession against a nearby foe, because the nail crumbles the moment it lands and rewards rapid close-range pressure over a single heavy cast. Ring the bell in the Finger Ruins of Rhia, then buy it from Count Ymir at the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. The Shadow of the Erdtree content is required before that region even exists on the map.
name: Glintstone Nail
effect: Fires a shattering magic nail

desc: Glintstone sorcery of Count Ymir, High Priest. One of the finger sorceries said to have been discovered in a hallowed ruin. Flings multiple magic nails that crumble during flight. Charging increases potency. Count Ymir boasts that this is mere child's play, an echo of a greater truth.
location: Purchased: Cathedral of Manus Metyr Glintstone Nails may be purchased from Count Ymir for 12,000 Runes after ringing the bell in the Finger Ruins of Rhia.
whatItIs: Count Ymir's finger sorcery that hurls a spread of magic nails forward, each one breaking apart and scattering shards over a small area as it reaches the target. Holding the charge button makes the burst hit harder, and it asks for a solid Intelligence investment to unlock.
whyItMatters: The multiple projectiles increase the chance of hitting a moving target compared to a single nail. A higher-Intelligence build gets more damage per cast while keeping the same short-range profile.
whenToUse: Aim it at a boss that strafes sideways, because the spread pattern gives each nail a better chance of grazing a moving target. It is bought from Count Ymir, sold at the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, unlocked by ringing the bell located in the Finger Ruins of Rhia, and both that site and the cathedral sit inside the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
name: Glintstone Nails
effect: Fires multiple shattering magic nails

desc: The most basic glintstone sorcery of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The glintstone serves as a conduit, launching magical projectiles at foes. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. This is a universal first step on the journey to true knowledge of sorcery.
location: Equipped: One of the starting spells of the Astrologer Origin. Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Scadu Altus x1 Sold for 1,000 Runes by Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins. x1 Sold for 1,000 Runes by Sorcerer Thops at Church of...
whatItIs: Fires a small glintstone bolt straight ahead. It is a Glintstone sorcery costing 7 FP and requiring 10 Intelligence. The cast is fast enough to use while running or dodging.
whyItMatters: It is the default starter bolt for a sorcery build, so a new caster can hit things in the first minutes without hunting for a better spell. The low FP cost means it can be spammed during exploration without draining the bar.
whenToUse: Equip it from the first grace if rolling the Astrologer Origin, or buy it for 1,000 Runes from Sorceress Sellen in Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, Academy of Raya Lucaria, or Scadu Altus. Swap it out once Intelligence crosses the threshold for a higher-cost sorcery.
name: Glintstone Pebble
effect: Fires magic projectiles from glintstone

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Fires three magic shooting stars that pursue the target. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Charging enhances potency. A sorcery of the Olivinus Conspectus, which attracts sorcerers from Sellia, Town of Sorcery.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Caelid / Roundtable Hold x1 Sold for 3,000 Runes by Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins. x1 Sold for 3,000 Runes by Sage Gowry after he has repaired the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle.
whatItIs: Launches three homing glintstone stars that track toward whatever is in front of the caster. It is a Glintstone sorcery costing 12 FP and requiring 12 Intelligence. Holding the cast button charges it for extra potency.
whyItMatters: The homing makes it forgiving to land on mobile enemies and bosses that sidestep, which helps a caster still learning range management. At 12 FP it sits between the cheap starter bolt and the expensive heavy hitters, giving a solid mid-range option through much of the base game.
whenToUse: Find it at any of Sorceress Sellen's shops in Limgrave, Liurnia of the Lakes, the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Caelid, or Roundtable Hold, or collect it from Sage Gowry once he mends the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle. Slot it in early and let the homing stars punish bosses that swing wide, especially when you charge the cast for added punch.
name: Glintstone Stars
effect: Fires three shooting stars that pursue foes

desc: Sorcery of the inquisitors of the tower, wielded as an incantation of the spiral. A swing of the arm releases a procession of golden arcs. Charging enhances potency. The arcs resemble barbs, a known symbol of coercive questioning.
location: Loot: Scadu Altus Found in an already opened chest within the pit in Moorth Ruins in a shrine guarded by three Inquisitors.
whatItIs: A sweeping arm motion releases a procession of golden arcs that travel outward. It is an incantation costing 12 FP and requiring 22 Faith. Charging the cast increases potency.
whyItMatters: The arcs hit in a wide band, making it useful against groups of enemies that cluster together. The Faith requirement keeps it accessible to a mid-level faith build without demanding a pure faith investment.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Loot it from an already opened chest in a pit within Moorth Ruins in Scadu Altus, in a shrine guarded by three Inquisitors. Equip it during a Faith build once the stat requirement is met and use it when enemies bunch up.
name: Golden Arcs
effect: Releases a procession of golden arcs with a swing of the arm

desc: An incantation of Erdtree Worship. Greatly increases lightning damage negation for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying, delaying the effect. This incantation was used by the knights of the Erdtree during the assault by the great ancient dragon Gransax, and the bitter War of the Ancient Dragons that followed.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Crumbling Farum Azula Drops from a Scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, near an Ancient Dragon.
whatItIs: Shields the caster and nearby allies with greatly increased lightning resistance. It is an Erdtree Worship incantation costing 30 FP and requiring 24 Faith. Holding the prayer delays the effect so the caster can time it to a specific moment.
whyItMatters: Lightning damage is a major threat in the later areas, so a dedicated resist buff turns a dangerous boss into a manageable one. It works on allies too, which makes it useful in a co-op session where a friend is also fighting a lightning-heavy enemy.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from a Scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace in Crumbling Farum Azula, near an Ancient Dragon. Cast it right before engaging a lightning-heavy boss or during a co-op fight where that damage type is the main threat.
name: Golden Lightning Fortification
effect: Greatly increases lightning resistance for self and allies

desc: An incantation of Erdtree Worship. Increases attack power and defense for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. This incantation has been taught to knights of the royal capital for generations, and knights sent on distant expeditions lean on it as a source of courage.
location: Loot: Mt. Gelmir Located inside the Corpse-Stench Shack east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity. Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater will also invade at this same spot.
whatItIs: Boosts both attack power and defense for the caster and nearby allies. It is an Erdtree Worship incantation costing 47 FP and requiring 25 Faith. Holding the prayer delays activation so the buff can be timed precisely.
whyItMatters: A combined offense and defense buff is rare in the incantation pool, making it a one-slot solution for a faith build that wants to hit harder and take less damage at the same time. The high FP cost means it should be saved for a boss fight rather than wasted on regular enemies.
whenToUse: Loot it from inside the Corpse-Stench Shack east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity in Mt. Gelmir, where Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater will also invade at that same spot. Activate it at the start of a boss fight or right before a phase transition when the damage exchange intensifies.
name: Golden Vow
effect: Increases attack and defense for self & allies

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries that manipulates gravitational forces. Fires a gravitational projectile that pulls in enemies before finally exploding. Charging increases potency. Said to have originated in the lightless dark far beyond—the home of the fallingstar beasts.
location: Dropped by the Fallingstar Beast found in the crater north of the Finger Ruins of Dheo.
whatItIs: Hurls a gravitational bolt that pulls enemies toward the caster before exploding. It is a Gravity sorcery costing 18 FP and requiring 36 Intelligence. Charging the cast increases potency.
whyItMatters: The pull effect disrupts an enemy's positioning, which is useful for keeping a boss in range or dragging a mobile foe into a follow-up attack. The high Intelligence requirement means it belongs on a well-built sorcery character rather than a mixed stat build.
whenToUse: Needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. It is dropped by the Fallingstar Beast found in the crater north of the Finger Ruins of Dheo. Use it on bosses that teleport or back away, pulling them into range before casting a heavier sorcery.
name: Gravitational Missile
effect: Fires a bolt of gravity that pulls in enemies

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries that manipulates gravitational forces. Fires a projectile of condensed gravitational force. Those struck by it will be pulled toward the caster. Charging enhances potency. A gravitational technique studied by the young Radahn. His master was an Alabaster Lord with skin of stone.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Academy of Raya Lucaria Acquired from defeating the Alabaster Lord that appears at the end of the graveyard, by the elevator that leads up to the Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace.
whatItIs: A bolt of condensed gravity that yanks whatever it hits back toward the caster. It belongs to the Gravity school, asks for a moderate Intelligence rating, and costs only a light amount of FP per cast. Keep the cast button held down and the pull strengthens considerably.
whyItMatters: The pull is strong enough to interrupt an enemy's attack animation and create an opening for a follow-up hit. At a moderate FP cost it can be cast repeatedly in a fight without draining the bar too fast.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from the Alabaster Lord at the end of the graveyard in Academy of Raya Lucaria, by the elevator that leads up to the Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace. Cast it when a boss starts a long wind-up or when an enemy is trying to retreat behind cover.
name: Gravity Well
effect: Pulls foes toward caster with gravity projectile

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The glintstone serves as a conduit, launching large magical projectiles at foes. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Those unworthy of the stone crown typically end their brief journey into sorcery here.
location: Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold Sold for 2,000 Runes by Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Preceptor Seluvis after giving either of them the Academy Scroll. Should the scroll be given to one of them and then have that instructor die...
whatItIs: A fat, dense bolt of glintstone energy that flies in a straight line and lands harder than the standard pebble. It sits in the Glintstone school, needs a fair chunk of Intelligence to wield, and can be fired in rapid succession while still moving. Pairs well with movement since the cast does not slow the caster down.
whyItMatters: It steps up from the starter bolt with noticeably more damage per cast while keeping the same simple aiming model. A sorcery build can live on this through the early and mid game before needing a higher-tier sorcery.
whenToUse: Once the Academy Scroll is handed over, Sorceress Sellen, Miriel, Pastor of Vows, or Preceptor Seluvis will sell it from their posts in Roundtable Hold, the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Liurnia of the Lakes, or Limgrave. Grab it the moment Intelligence clears the mid-teens and it becomes a dependable range weapon until a heavier option shows up.
name: Great Glintstone Shard
effect: Fires larger magic projectiles from glintstone

desc: Superior incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Greatly heals HP for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. The Two Fingers has high hopes for the Tarnished; that even if they should be wounded, even should they fall, they will continue to fight for their duty.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 9,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Altus Plateau. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for...
whatItIs: Light floods out from the caster and refills the health of everyone standing nearby, making it a wide-area mend rather than a single-target one. It carries the Two Fingers school, so a fair amount of Faith is needed to channel it and the FP cost runs high. Hold the cast button and the prayer stays charged, letting the caster pick the exact moment it blooms.
whyItMatters: The big heal pool covers a boss phase that drops half the health bar in one burst, which a smaller heal cannot survive. At 15 Faith it is within reach of most faith builds without a dedicated stat investment.
whenToUse: Buy it for 9,000 Runes from Brother Corhyn in Roundtable Hold, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or Mountaintops of the Giants after he moves to Altus Plateau. Hold the cast through a boss recovery window and release when the health bar is below half.
name: Great Heal
effect: Greatly heals HP for self and nearby allies

desc: Sorcery of the claymen who served as priests in the ancient dynasty. Produces a gigantic magical bubble that drifts towards foes before it naturally ruptures. Charging increases the delay before the bubble pops. The claymen search for lost oracles within their bubbles.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Siofra River Acquired from felling a Scarab surrounded by Claymen inside of a large building on the southwestern quarter of the level with the Dragonkin Soldier. The level can be accessed from Siofra river through a Portal found on some ruins south of the Worshippers' Woods Site...
whatItIs: Spits a large magic bubble that drifts slowly toward enemies before rupturing. It is a sorcery costing 16 FP and requiring 25 Intelligence and 18 Arcane. Charging the cast delays the pop, giving the caster more time to position.
