whyItMatters: The slow drift means the bubble connects even if the target moves, making it a forgiving area option in the sorcery pool. The dual stat requirement of Intelligence and Arcane is unusual and suits a hybrid caster who levels both.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from a Scarab surrounded by Claymen inside a large building on the southwestern quarter of the level with the Dragonkin Soldier, accessed from Siofra River through a Portal on some ruins south of the Worshippers' Woods Site of Grace. Wait for a group to cluster, then release the bubble so it drifts into the middle of them.
name: Great Oracular Bubble
effect: Launches a large magic bubble

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Creates a defensive arch of larger magic glintblades overhead, which automatically attack nearby foes. Used by the enchanted troll knights. They were the comrades of the young Rennala, bound by oath.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating Bols, Carian Knight in the Cuckoo's Evergaol.
whatItIs: Conjures a defensive arch of larger magic glintblades overhead that automatically attack nearby foes. It is a sorcery costing 30 FP and requiring 29 Intelligence. Once active, the blades handle themselves without further input.
whyItMatters: The automatic targeting means it can cover a fight while the caster focuses on dodging or casting another spell. At 29 Intelligence it is a mid-game sorcery that rewards a committed magic build over a mixed one.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from Bols, Carian Knight in the Cuckoo's Evergaol in Liurnia of the Lakes. Cast it at the start of a multi-enemy room or when a boss has a long cast animation, then step aside and let the blades work.
name: Greatblade Phalanx
effect: Forms a defensive arch of larger magic glintblades

desc: Superior incantation of Dragon Communion. Channels the power of Greyoll, the Elder Dragon. An incantation of legendary status. Transforms caster into a dragon to emit a terrible roar, reducing the attack power and defense of nearby enemies. Greyoll was the mother of all dragons, dwarfing all who stood before her like a looming mountain.
location: Dragon Communion: Caelid Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 3 Dragon Hearts after felling Elder Dragon Greyoll.
whatItIs: Channels the power of Greyoll, the Elder Dragon, to emit a terrible roar that reduces the attack power and defense of nearby enemies. It is a Dragon Communion incantation costing 50 FP in two slots and requiring 28 Faith and 17 Arcane.
whyItMatters: Weakening a boss's offense and defense simultaneously opens a window to deal damage without taking as much in return. The two-slot cost is a big ask, so it suits a faith build that has room in the incantation bar.
whenToUse: Head to the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and trade a few Dragon Hearts at the altar, but only after you have felled Elder Dragon Greyoll. Loosen a boss's guard with it right before it winds up a devastating attack, or slam it into a crowd that is closing in fast.
name: Greyoll's Roar
effect: Emits the roar of Elder Dragon Greyoll

desc: Superior incantation taught by Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Creates beast claws that rend surroundings with shockwaves. Long ago, Gurranq was a beast of such terrifying ferocity that his former name meant "Death of the Demigods."
location: Quest Item: Bestial Sanctum, Greyoll's Dragonbarrow Gurranq's Beast Claw is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the eight Deathroot. (However, only after Gurranq has been calmed down after he turns hostile on the player's return to him after consuming the fourth Deathroot.)
whatItIs: Creates beast claws that rend the surroundings with shockwaves. It is a bestial incantation costing 21 FP and requiring 15 Faith. The shockwave hits in a wide area around the caster.
whyItMatters: The wide-area shockwave is effective against groups of enemies that close in, making it a good crowd-clearing option for a faith build. The low Faith requirement means it is accessible early without a dedicated stat investment.
whenToUse: It is rewarded by Gurranq after giving him the eight Deathroot in the Bestial Sanctum at Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, but only after he has been calmed down following the fourth Deathroot. Use it when three or more enemies are within melee range and a single-target spell would waste FP.
name: Gurranq's Beast Claw
effect: Creates beast claws to rend surroundings with shockwaves

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Heals HP for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. The Two Fingers has high hopes for the Tarnished; that even if they should be wounded, even should they fall, they will continue to fight for their duty.
location: Equipped: Heal is a starting spell for the Prophet origin. Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from...
whatItIs: Soft light restores the vitality of the caster and every ally in close range, and holding the cast button delays when the effect blooms. It sits in the Two Fingers school, needs only a modest Faith stat, and the FP cost stays low. A Prophet origin character starts with it ready to cast, so it is on hand from the opening moment.
whyItMatters: It covers a single heavy hit or a short burst of damage from a boss, which is all a new character needs to survive the first few fights. The low Faith requirement and moderate FP cost make it a safe heal for any faith-leaning build.
whenToUse: If the Prophet Origin is the character being rolled, it is already equipped from the first step. Otherwise, Brother Corhyn sells it in Roundtable Hold, on the Altus Plateau, in Leyndell, Royal Capital, or on the Mountaintops of the Giants for a modest sum of Runes. Hold the cast while a boss recovers and let the heal bloom just before the next swing lands.
name: Heal
effect: Heals HP for you and nearby allies

desc: An Erdtree incantation discovered in the realm of shadow. Fires a projectile toward distant allies that greatly restores HP on contact. Even when far beyond, far out of sight, the Erdtree will surely give us its blessing.
location: Loot: Scadu Altus North of Moorth Ruins there are two small bodies of water. At the northern edge of the southern body of water is a small cave tunnel with a Miranda Blossom and three Perfumers, with the incantation lying under a glowing tree at the end.
whatItIs: Healing light travels outward as a focused bolt that seeks a distant ally and floods their health on impact. It belongs to the Erdtree school, so a solid Faith stat is the gate and the FP cost mirrors that of a heavier close-range heal. No melee range is required, which makes it a natural fit whenever the target is out of arm's reach.
whyItMatters: Healing a friend who is across the arena removes the risk of getting pulled into the boss's attack to reach them. The Faith requirement is modest, so a hybrid build can slot it without sacrificing a damage incantation.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is needed. Loot it in Scadu Altus, north of Moorth Ruins, at the northern edge of the southern body of water where a small cave tunnel holds a Miranda Blossom and three Perfumers, with the incantation under a glowing tree at the end. Fire it at a co-op partner who is taking damage while the caster is still positioned for the next attack.
name: Heal from Afar
effect: Greatly heals HP for distant allies the spell reaches

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons a bolt of lightning to strike foes from above. This incantation can be cast repeatedly. Long ago, Godwyn the Golden defeated the ancient dragon Fortissax, and befriended his fallen foe — an event that gave rise to the ancient dragon cult in the capital.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 7,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then...
whatItIs: Calls down a lightning bolt from above to strike a target. It is a dragon cult incantation costing 12 FP and requiring 24 Faith. It can be cast repeatedly, making it a rapid-fire option.
whyItMatters: The bolt hits from above, so it connects even when the target is behind a low wall or crouching. At 12 FP it is cheap enough to spam on regular enemies while saving bigger incantations for bosses.
whenToUse: Brother Corhyn and Miriel, Pastor of Vows both carry it for a healthy sum of Runes in Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, the Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or the Mountaintops of the Giants, but only after you hand them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook. Fire it into open clearings where a squad is bunched up and the falling bolt can reach overhead without clipping a roof.
name: Honed Bolt
effect: Strikes foe with lightning bolt from above

desc: Incantation originating from the maddening Three Fingers. Releases a maddening shriek that causes madness buildup in foes nearby. This incantation also causes madness buildup in the caster and makes enemies more likely to target them. It is said that the sickness of the flame of frenzy began with Shabriri, the most reviled man in all history.
location: Loot: Frenzy-Flaming Tower (Liurnia of the Lakes) Howl of Shabriri is located in a treasure chest on the second floor of the Tower, located southeast of the Grand Lift of Dectus.
whatItIs: Shrieks a maddening sound that builds up madness in nearby foes. It is a frenzy incantation costing 21 FP and requiring 33 Faith. It also causes madness buildup in the caster and draws enemy aggro toward them.
whyItMatters: Forcing a boss into a madness state can interrupt their patterns and create a damage window. The self-madness and aggro pull are trade-offs that make it a high-risk, high-reward option for a dedicated faith build.
whenToUse: Loot it from a treasure chest on the second floor of the Frenzy-Flaming Tower in Liurnia of the Lakes, southeast of the Grand Lift of Dectus. Cast it when a boss has just finished a heavy attack and is in a short recovery, then step out of the madness radius before it ticks.
name: Howl of Shabriri
effect: Shrieks, building up madness in nearby foes

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. Enchants the shield held in the left hand with the light of regression, increasing all forms of non-Physical damage negation and ailment resistance. Two concepts form the basis for Golden Order fundamentalism. One is the law of regression, to which this incantation relates.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold by Brother Corhyn for 10,000 Runes after telling Goldmask that Radagon is Marika. Should Corhyn die but before purchasing this Incantation after solving Goldmask's puzzle, then the player can still purchase it...
whatItIs: Enchants the shield in the left hand with the light of regression, increasing non-physical damage negation and ailment resistance. It is a Golden Order incantation costing 15 FP and requiring 19 Intelligence and 19 Faith.
whyItMatters: A shield already blocks physical damage well, and this adds a layer against magic, fire, lightning, and holy hits that would otherwise get through. The dual stat requirement of Intelligence and Faith suits a hybrid build that carries both sorceries and incantations.
whenToUse: Brother Corhyn parts with it in Roundtable Hold, in the Mountaintops of the Giants, and later in Leyndell, Royal Capital, but the unlock gate is telling Goldmask that Radagon is Marika. It fits a caster who carries a physical shield into fights full of bleed, poison, or fire, so cast it right before the first exchange and let the extra ailment negation carry the caster through hits that would otherwise lock the guard down.
name: Immutable Shield
effect: Increases left-hand shield's affinity/ailment resistance

desc: Sorcery of those who abandoned the practice of incantations after devout faith rewarded them with only despair. Summons the Scadutree's impenetrable thorns from the ground. This sorcery can be used repeatedly. The image of the twisted Scadutree is an edict: Denounce their ways. Do them harm. For they have abandoned us.
location: Loot: Scadu Altus Impenetrable Thorns is found in the Shadow Keep. Before ascending the stairs to the bridge leading to Messmer's tower, drop down to a balcony with a single Man-Bat. The sorcery is located on a corpse against the wall.
whatItIs: Rips a cluster of thorns up through the earth around the caster, impaling anything that drifts too close. It is a Thorn sorcery with a moderate FP cost and a solid Faith requirement to cast. Fire it in open spaces where the thorns have room to spread and punish enemies that charge in.
whyItMatters: The thorns erupt from the ground, which means they hit enemies at the caster's feet without needing to aim a projectile. A faith-leaning build can use it as a cheap area denial tool in tight corridors.
whenToUse: The sorcery is locked to characters running the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Find it in the Shadow Keep in Scadu Altus: before ascending the stairs to the bridge leading to Messmer's tower, drop down to a balcony with a single Man-Bat and take the sorcery from a corpse against the wall. Cast it when enemies are within a few steps and the caster needs them pushed back.
name: Impenetrable Thorns
effect: Summons the Scadutree's impenetrable thorns from the earth

desc: Incantation originating from the maddening Three Fingers. Causes the yellow flame of frenzy to blaze from the caster's eyes. The caster then latches onto foes, spreading the madness. This incantation also causes buildup of madness in the caster, and is only effective against Tarnished. To gaze into one another's eyes is truly the most intimate form of human contact.
location: Loot: Subterranean Shunning-Grounds (Leyndell, Royal Capital/Leyndell, Ashen Capital) Inescapable Frenzy is found on top of a coffin near the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription, which can be reached after defeating Mohg, the Omen.
whatItIs: Latches onto a target and spreads madness from the caster's blazing eyes. It is a frenzy incantation costing 22 FP and requiring 21 Faith. It also builds up madness in the caster and is only effective against Tarnished.
whyItMatters: Because it only works on Tarnished, it is a dedicated player-versus-player tool rather than a general damage spell. The latching effect removes the target's ability to kite, which flips a ranged advantage.
whenToUse: Loot it from a coffin near the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds under Leyndell, Royal Capital or Leyndell, Ashen Capital, reachable after defeating Mohg, the Omen. Use it in a player-versus-player session when the opponent has a ranged advantage and needs to be forced into melee.
name: Inescapable Frenzy
effect: Latches onto foes to spread madness

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons a lightning spear while also manifesting ancient dragon crests. On throwing the spear, the crests will launch additional spears. Charge to increase the number of crests and add a bolt of lightning to impact. An incantation that was taught only to the most accomplished knights, and now a lost art in the Lands Between.
location: Loot: Scorpion River Catacombs After arriving in the room with a spiked falling roof, keep to the right to find a ladder in one of the small safe spots around the corner (in the second half of the room) and climb up it. Cross the bridge to the right and then, after waiting for the Death Blight...
whatItIs: A chargeable incantation of the dragon cult that hurls a lightning spear forward while ancient dragon crests erupt and each launch an additional bolt. Charging the cast summons more crests and adds a lightning strike at the impact point. It costs 29 FP and asks for 36 Faith.
whyItMatters: The extra projectiles make it a strong answer to groups of enemies in narrow corridors and a reliable single-target nuke when fully charged. A Faith build that already runs mid-range incantations will slot it in as a higher-damage option against clustered foes or single bosses.
whenToUse: This spell needs the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. It drops as loot in the Scorpion River Catacombs; after arriving in the room with the spiked falling roof, keep to the right and find a ladder in one of the small safe spots around the corner, then climb it and cross the bridge to the right.
name: Knight's Lightning Spear
effect: Hurls lightning spear while firing additional spears from ancient dragon crests

desc: Incantation originating from Scadutree avatars. Creates a hail of golden projectiles which are fired toward foes after a brief delay. This incantation channels the force of the Scadutree's power, and its gold is accompanied by shadow.
location: Trade: Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold. The remembrance is acquired by defeating the Scadutree Avatar. After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to duplicate it....
whatItIs: An incantation that channels the power of the Scadutree and fires a hail of golden projectiles at whatever is in front after a brief delay. It is a Faith spell with no charge step, costing 40 FP and 58 Faith to equip.
whyItMatters: The spread of golden projectiles makes it a solid crowd-control tool in open arenas where a single beam would miss. A high-Faith build that wants a one-button area effect without charging will find it a dependable option against swarms and grouped adds.
whenToUse: The incantation is tied entirely to the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower drops from the Scadutree Avatar, and Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold will exchange it for the incantation. A Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can also be used to duplicate the remembrance.
name: Land of Shadow (Incantation)
effect: Fires a hail of golden projectiles toward foes

desc: Incantation that channels the power of the ancient dragon Lansseax. Creates a red-lightning glaive and sweeps the area from above. This attack unleashes trails of lightning. Lansseax was the sister of Fortissax. It is said that she took the form of a human to commune with the knights as a priestess of the ancient dragon cult.
location: Lansseax's Glaive is obtained by defeating Ancient Dragon Lansseax on the Altus Plateau, south of the Rampartside Path site of grace outside of the wall to the Capital Outskirts.
whatItIs: A dragon-cult incantation that summons a red-lightning glaive overhead and sweeps it across the area below. It leaves trails of lightning along the sweep path. The spell costs 22 FP and requires 40 Faith.
whyItMatters: The wide sweeping arc hits everything in a line, which makes it useful against groups that are spread out along a wall or corridor. A Faith caster who wants a single-target-to-light-area spell without a charge step will find it a dependable mid-range option.
whenToUse: Defeat Ancient Dragon Lansseax on the Altus Plateau, south of the Rampartside Path site of grace outside the wall to the Capital Outskirts, and the incantation drops as a reward. It fits a build that is already running Faith as the primary stat by the time the Altus Plateau opens up.
name: Lansseax's Glaive
effect: Sweeps from above with red lightning glaive

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. One of the key fundamentals. Manifests a small ring of causality within that allows the caster to automatically retaliate upon receiving a certain number of blows. The fundamentalists describe the Golden Order through the powers of regression and causality. Causality is the pull between meanings; that which links all things in a chain of relation.
location: Given by Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after defeating Mohg, Lord of Blood and choosing to talk "About the Lord of Blood's Cocoon". Can also be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks for 5,000 Runes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.
whatItIs: A defensive incantation that manifests a small ring of causality around the caster. Once a set number of hits have landed on the caster, the ring automatically retaliates against whatever struck. It costs 22 FP and needs 29 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: It turns a passive defensive posture into an automatic counter-attack, which is useful for builds that want to tank hits and punish without reacting manually. An Intelligence-focused build that already leans on Golden Order incantations can slot it in as a safety net without needing a separate stat investment.
whenToUse: Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing gives it after defeating Mohg, Lord of Blood and choosing to talk "About the Lord of Blood's Cocoon". It can also be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks for 5,000 Runes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. Either route lands in the mid-to-late game.
name: Law of Causality
effect: Retaliates upon receiving a number of blows

desc: Incantation of the Golden Order fundamentalists. One of the key fundamentals. Heals all negative statuses, dispels special effects, and reveals mimicry in all its forms. The fundamentalists describe the Golden Order through the powers of regression and causality. Regression is the pull of meaning; that all things yearn eternally to converge.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 10,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then...
whatItIs: An all-purpose cleanup incantation that heals all negative statuses and dispels special effects on the caster. It also exposes any mimicry in its true form. The spell costs 55 FP and asks for 37 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: A single cast clears every ailment and dispels special effects at once, which removes the need to carry separate cure incantations for each status type. A caster who wants one button to fix any debuff will find it a slot-saver in any build.
whenToUse: Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows sells it for 10,000 Runes at Roundtable Hold, in Liurnia of the Lakes, on the Altus Plateau, in Leyndell, Royal Capital, or on the Mountaintops of the Giants, after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia. It is a good pick-up once the build has enough FP to spare for a dedicated cleanup slot.
name: Law of Regression
effect: Heals all ailments and dispels all special effects

desc: The strength of Miquella upon his deific return, wielded as an incantation. Annihilates foes with a pillar of light. Miquella sought to accept all that was and would be, but found one that refused to be embraced. No wonder, as one god and one king consort, is all the world needs.
location: Trade: Remembrance of a God and a Lord Trade with Finger Reader Enia. Alternatively, use one of the belled Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate the remembrance (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).
whatItIs: The pillar-of-light incantation tied to Miquella's deific return. It annihilates everything in a column of light at the target point. The spell occupies two incantation slots, costs 48 FP, and demands 72 Faith.
whyItMatters: The column hits a wide area and deals heavy damage, making it a strong answer to bosses that stay in one spot or to dense groups of enemies. A Faith build that has room for a two-slot spell and the Faith stat to back it will find it a high-damage nuke.
whenToUse: This is a Shadow of the Erdtree expansion spell. The Remembrance of a God and a Lord is traded with Finger Reader Enia for the incantation, or a Wandering Mausoleum can duplicate the remembrance. Only one copy is available per playthrough through either method.
name: Light of Miquella
effect: Annihilates foes with a pillar of light

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Increases lightning damage negation. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Follow the path that has been set for you, and you will make enemies of all others: the monks, the sorcerers, the ancient dragon knights, and the scions of gold. Heed me — the Lands Between offers no welcome to the Tarnished.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Altus Plateau. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for...
whatItIs: Raises lightning damage negation for the caster, and it can be cast while in motion. It is a Two Fingers incantation. It costs 20 FP and asks for only 10 Faith.
whyItMatters: Lightning is a common damage type from bosses and enemies, so a dedicated negation buff shaves real numbers off every hit taken. A Faith build that fights in areas heavy with lightning enemies or bosses will feel the difference immediately.
whenToUse: Brother Corhyn offers it at the Altus Plateau, Roundtable Hold, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and the Mountaintops of the Giants for a set rune price once he has settled. If he dies before the deal goes through, the Twin Maiden Husks carry it as a backup. Slot it in early for any stretch heavy with lightning enemies.
name: Lightning Fortification
effect: Increases lightning damage negation

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons a lightning spear and hurls it before the caster. Charging causes a lightning bolt to strike the point of impact. Long ago, Godwyn the Golden defeated the ancient dragon Fortissax, and befriended his fallen foe — an event that gave rise to the ancient dragon cult in the capital.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 6,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then...
whatItIs: An incantation that hurls a lightning spear in front of the caster. Charging the cast adds a lightning bolt that strikes the impact point. It costs 18 FP and asks for 17 Faith.
whyItMatters: The charge step gives it a two-tier identity: a quick poke for small enemies or a delayed bolt for bosses and tougher foes. A Faith build that wants a reliable ranged option from early on will find it one of the first solid incantations to equip.
whenToUse: Hand the Dragon Cult Prayerbook to either Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows, and the incantation unlocks at Liurnia of the Lakes, Roundtable Hold, the Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, or the Mountaintops of the Giants. A Faith build can slot it in early for a cheap, reliable poke. Hold the cast to draw a lightning bolt onto the impact point for extra punch.
name: Lightning Spear
effect: Hurls lightning spear before caster

desc: One of the incantations of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Summons a bolt of lightning that scatters and spreads around the surrounding area. This incantation can be cast repeatedly. Ancestors of the modern dragons, the ancient dragons had scales of Gravel Stone and wielded lightning as their weapon. It is said that they once attacked Leyndell, the Royal Capital.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Weeping Peninsula Lightning Strike is received upon defeating the Scarab at the bottom of the ravine splitting the Weeping Peninsula region in half. The stone platforms on either side of this can be used to descend safely. Note that it's surrounded by large bats and that...
whatItIs: The area-denial version of the dragon cult's lightning kit. It summons a bolt of lightning that scatters and spreads across the surrounding area after impact. It costs 19 FP and requires 28 Faith.
whyItMatters: The bolt scatters outward from the landing point, which puts pressure on adds that cluster around a boss or on a target that cannot be kited. A Faith build wanting a short-range area effect that does not demand a wind-up will feel the value here. It casts instantly, so it slots in cleanly between dodge rolls.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from the Scarab at the bottom of the ravine splitting the Weeping Peninsula region in half. The stone platforms on either side of the ravine can be used to descend safely, and large bats guard the area. It is one of the earliest incantations a Faith build can pick up.
name: Lightning Strike
effect: Summons lightning bolt that spreads from impact

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. Used by hunters of Those Who Live in Death. Creates an image of Order, dealing holy damage to nearby foes. This incantation is especially damaging to Those Who Live in Death. Any felled by this incantation cannot be revived. The role of the hunters is to stamp out defiled reason – all for the perfection of the Golden Order.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold Sold by D, Hunter of the Dead for 2,500 Runes after speaking to Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum.
whatItIs: One incantation from the Golden Order that creates an image of Order and deals holy damage to nearby foes. It is especially damaging to Those Who Live in Death, and any enemy it fells cannot be revived. The spell costs 17 FP and needs 17 Intelligence and 17 Faith.
whyItMatters: The anti-revival property makes it a strong answer to enemies that would otherwise keep coming back, and the holy damage bonus hits undead and death-type foes for more than a standard incantation. A build that mixes Intelligence and Faith will find it a niche but valuable tool against specific enemy types.
whenToUse: D, Hunter of the Dead sells it at Roundtable Hold for 2,500 Runes after speaking to Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum. It fits a build that is heading toward Leyndell and wants a reliable answer for the undead-heavy encounters along the way.
name: Litany of Proper Death
effect: Creates image of Order to deal holy damage

desc: Incantation bestowed by the Two Fingers upon the Tarnished deemed worthy of becoming a lord. Alleviates buildup of poison, blood loss, and sleep for the caster and nearby allies. Additionally, cures poison. Hold to continue praying and delay activation.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Lord's Aid is sold for 2,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Two Fingers' Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of...
whatItIs: Lord's Aid is a Two Fingers incantation that alleviates the buildup of poison, blood loss, and sleep for the caster and nearby allies. Holding the cast delays activation, and it also cures poison immediately. The spell costs only 9 FP and 12 Faith.
whyItMatters: The low FP cost and wide coverage make it a cheap insurance policy for any build that wants to keep poison and bleed off the character without spending a full heal. A Faith build with allies in co-op or a build that keeps getting hit with status ailments will find it a slot-saver.
whenToUse: Hand the Two Fingers' Prayerbook to Brother Corhyn or to Miriel, Pastor of Vows, and Lord's Aid appears for sale at Roundtable Hold, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and Mountaintops of the Giants. Activate it the moment poison, bleed, or sleep buildup starts climbing on the party, because in co-op one bad status can cascade into a wipe that nobody recovers from. The FP cost is so low that a Faith build can hold it in the incantation slot from the very first area without the resource ever feeling tight.
name: Lord's Aid
effect: Alleviates poison / blood loss / sleep buildup for self and allies

desc: Incantation taught to Gideon the All-Knowing by the Two Fingers. Greatly increases holy damage negation for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. Gideon gained true knowledge after his long exchange with the Two Fingers — discovering all had been broken long ago; that the trembling fingers, bent with age, and the Erdtree itself, were no exception.
location: Quest Item / Purchase: Roundtable Hold Received from Gideon after discussing the haligtree roots, once Malenia, Blade of Miquella has been defeated. Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 3,500 Runes if the player does not talk to Gideon about the roots before unleashing the Rune of Death.
whatItIs: The charged Two Fingers buff for holy resistance. It greatly increases holy damage negation for the caster and nearby allies, with holding the cast to delay activation. The spell costs 30 FP and asks for 27 Faith.
whyItMatters: Holy damage shows up in a long stretch of later encounters, so a dedicated negation buff takes real pressure off the health bar during those fights. It covers allies as well, which makes it a co-op staple for Faith builds. A caster heading into the Royal Capital or the Mountaintops will notice the difference the moment a holy beam lands.
whenToUse: Gideon gives it after discussing the haligtree roots, once Malenia, Blade of Miquella has been defeated. If the roots are not discussed before unleashing the Rune of Death, the Twin Maiden Husks will sell it for 3,500 Runes at Roundtable Hold. Slot it in when holy-damage bosses start showing up and leave it equipped through the capital arc.
name: Lord's Divine Fortification
effect: Greatly increases holy damage negation including allies

desc: Incantation bestowed by the Two Fingers upon the Tarnished deemed worthy of becoming a lord. Heals a massive amount of HP for the caster and nearby allies. Hold to continue praying and delay activation. Tarnished—O, Tarnished! Seek the Erdtree and stand before Marika, its Queen. Become the Elden Lord!
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 8,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows, after giving either of them the Two Fingers' Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and...
whatItIs: Restores a massive amount of HP for the caster and nearby allies in a single cast. Holding the cast delays activation. The spell costs 55 FP and requires 20 Faith.
whyItMatters: The large heal covers the gap that smaller incantations leave open, especially in co-op or in fights where HP has been chewed down by multiple enemies. A Faith build that wants one button to reset the health bar will find it a dependable emergency option.
whenToUse: Once Miriel, Pastor of Vows or Brother Corhyn receives the Two Fingers' Prayerbook, Lord's Heal appears in the vendor inventory at Liurnia of the Lakes, the Altus Plateau, Leyndell, Royal Capital, the Mountaintops of the Giants, and Roundtable Hold. Because the FP cost is substantial, a caster should hold off until the build has breathing room in the FP pool. In co-op it restores the caster and every nearby ally with one cast, making it a strong panic option when both parties are low.
name: Lord's Heal
effect: Massively heals HP for self and nearby allies

desc: Sorcery used by Royal Knight Loretta. Creates a magic greatbow and fires a great arrow. Charging enhances potency. Hold to keep the great arrow nocked. It is said that the bow was Loretta's favored weapon.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating the apparition of Royal Knight Loretta guarding the Royal Moongazing Grounds of Caria Manor.
whatItIs: Conjures a magic greatbow and fires a great arrow at the target. Charging the cast enhances the arrow's potency, and holding it keeps the arrow nocked. It costs 24 FP and asks for 26 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The single strong arrow is a clean, easy-to-aim option for players who want a reliable ranged hit without the complexity of multi-projectile sorceries. An Intelligence build that wants a straightforward single-target spell will find it a solid early-to-mid option.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from the apparition of Royal Knight Loretta guarding the Royal Moongazing Grounds of Caria Manor in Liurnia of the Lakes. It fits a build that has committed to Intelligence by the time Caria Manor opens up.
name: Loretta's Greatbow
effect: Fires great arrow from a magic greatbow

desc: Sorcery used by Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree. Creates a magic greatbow and fires four great arrows simultaneously. Charging enhances potency. Hold to keep the great arrows nocked. Developed by Loretta after her long, bloody journey to seek out a place where the Albinaurics could live in peace.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Miquella's Haligtree Acquired from defeating Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree standing guard at the Haligtree Promenade.
whatItIs: Conjures a magic greatbow and fires four great arrows at once. Charging the cast enhances the arrows' potency, and holding it keeps them nocked. It costs 39 FP and demands 46 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The four-arrow spread covers a wider area than a single shot, making it useful against groups or against a boss that is moving. A high-Intelligence build that has the FP to spare will find it a satisfying area-control option.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree standing guard at the Haligtree Promenade in Miquella's Haligtree. It is a late-game pick-up that rewards a build that has been investing in Intelligence from early on.
name: Loretta's Mastery
effect: Fires four great arrows from a magic greatbow at once

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Alleviates buildup of sleep and madness. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. The Carian knights never waver.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating Preceptor Miriam in the inverted version of Carian Study Hall.
whatItIs: Alleviates the buildup of sleep and madness on the caster. It can be cast while moving, so it does not lock the character in place. It costs 10 FP and asks for 17 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: Sleep and madness are two of the more disruptive ailments in the game, and a quick cast of Lucidity removes the buildup without needing a dedicated incantation slot. A caster who wants to cover both sleep and madness with one button will find it a cheap insurance policy.
whenToUse: It drops guaranteed from Preceptor Miriam in the inverted version of Carian Study Hall in Liurnia of the Lakes. Equip it once the build is running sorceries and the inverted Study Hall is reachable, and keep it in the loadout for any area with sleep or madness attacks.
name: Lucidity
effect: Alleviates buildup of sleep and madness

desc: One of the sorceries of the Carian royal family. Summons a mass of magic that fires projectiles over a wide area. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Charging extends duration. Said to have been taught by the Crystalians to mark the swearing of the old concord.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating Preceptor Miriam in the normal version of Carian Study Hall.
whatItIs: Summons a mass of magic that fires projectiles across a wide area. Charging the cast extends the duration of the rain. It can be cast while moving, and the spell costs 18 FP and asks for 15 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The wide spray of projectiles puts sustained pressure on anything that crowds the screen, from groups of enemies to a boss weaving through a corridor. An Intelligence build wanting a simple area effect without precise aiming will get a lot of use out of it. Charging the cast stretches the duration, which adds another layer of control in longer fights.
whenToUse: Defeat Preceptor Miriam in Carian Study Hall (the normal version, found in Liurnia of the Lakes) to receive it as a guaranteed drop. It casts while moving and the charged version lasts longer, so it fits any moment where a crowd is closing from multiple angles. A pure Int build can slot it early and keep it loaded through the mid game without breaking the FP budget.
name: Magic Downpour
effect: Summon a magic mass that sprays projectiles over area

desc: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful. Increases magic damage negation. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Follow the path that has been set for you, and you will make enemies of all others: the monks, the sorcerers, the ancient dragon knights, and the scions of gold. Heed me — the Lands Between offers no welcome to the Tarnished.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 3,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn. Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving...
whatItIs: Raises magic damage negation for the caster and can be cast while moving. It is a Two Fingers incantation. The cost is 20 FP with a Faith requirement of just 10.
whyItMatters: Magic is a heavily represented sorcery damage type across the Lands Between, which means a resistance buff trims a meaningful chunk off nearly every caster hit. A Faith build fighting through zones packed with sorcerers or projectile enemies will feel the relief immediately. It is cheap to cast and refreshes on the fly, so keeping it up costs almost nothing in effort.
whenToUse: Pick it up from Brother Corhyn, who stocks it at the Mountaintops of the Giants, Leyndell, Royal Capital, the Altus Plateau, and Roundtable Hold. If Corhyn has fallen before the coin changes hands, the Twin Maiden Husks stock it at the same price. Equip it before any encounter dominated by magic arrows or beams, because a Faith build with low negation will feel every hit without it.
name: Magic Fortification
effect: Increases magic damage negation

desc: An old sorcery of the Carian Royal Family. Creates a sigil overhead, from which an enemy-seeking glintblade appears after a brief delay. This sorcery can be used while in motion. Charging increases the delay. Said to be the prototype of the sword-phalanx sorceries wielded by royal enchanted knights
location: Equipped: A starting spell for the Prisoner origin. Purchase: Liurnia of the Lakes / Roundtable Hold Sold for 3,000 Runes by Miriel, Pastor of Vows. Should Miriel die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price,...
whatItIs: Places a sigil overhead, from which an enemy-seeking glintblade appears after a brief delay. Charging the cast increases the delay before the blade strikes. It costs 12 FP and asks for 14 Intelligence.
whyItMatters: The homing behavior means it does not require precise aiming, which makes it a forgiving option for new casters. A low-Intelligence build that wants a reliable projectile spell without the targeting pressure of a beam or arrow will find it an easy early slot.
whenToUse: It comes equipped for the Prisoner origin, and it can also be bought from Miriel, Pastor of Vows at Roundtable Hold or in Liurnia of the Lakes. If Miriel is gone first, the Twin Maiden Husks carry it at the same cost. It is a forgiving early pick that rewards patience with its delayed projectile.
name: Magic Glintblade
effect: Creates sigil that forms a projectile glintblade after delay

desc: One of the incantations of Dragon Communion. Transforms caster into a wyrm to spew magma breath. Allows one follow-up attack. Those who have performed the Dragon Communion will find their humanity slowly slipping away. Once they fully succumb to their fate, they are left no more than wyrms that crawl the earth.
location: Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart after defeating the Magma Wyrm south of Fort Laiedd at...
whatItIs: Dragon Communion incantation that morphs the caster into a wyrm and floods the area ahead with a broad stream of molten rock. A single follow-up strike is permitted once the breath exhausts itself. It calls for a solid Faith baseline plus a modest Arcane score, so a dragon-speaker who has sprinkled some Arcane into the build can wield it without straining.
whyItMatters: The magma breath covers a broad arc in front of the caster, which puts pressure on anything clustered at close range. A build that can spare a Dragon Heart and wants a visceral close-range incantation will get a lot of mileage from it. It pairs well with other Dragon Communion spells that share the same resource.
whenToUse: It is acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak, for 1 Dragon Heart after defeating the Magma Wyrm south of Fort Laiedd. It fits a build that has access to Dragon Communion and wants a close-range damage option.
name: Magma Breath
effect: Channels wyrm to spew magma breath

desc: One of the sorceries developed from the magma of Mt. Gelmir. Fires a lump of magma that explodes on contact. Charging enhances potency. After discovering the ancient hexes of Gelmir, Rykard, son of Queen Rennala, brought them back into practical use as new forms of sorcery.
location: Quest Item: Volcano Manor Acquired from Tanith after successfully felling the first assassination target, Old Knight Istvan. Loot: Volcano Manor If Old Knight Istvan is assassinated after Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is killed, will be found inside the Drawing Room within Volcano Manor.
whatItIs: A sorcery from the volcanic lore of Mt. Gelmir that hurls a molten lump which detonates the moment it strikes anything. It asks for a solid Intelligence floor with a touch of Faith, and holding the cast button before release packs the blast with noticeably more force.
whyItMatters: The splash on impact makes it useful in tight corridors and against clustered foes where one blast clips several enemies at once. A caster leaning into Fire damage or a mixed Faith-Intelligence build can slot it in without heavy investment. The charge option adds a burst-damage moment against a single large target standing still.
whenToUse: Tanith hands it over after the first assassination target, Old Knight Istvan, is felled at Volcano Manor. If Old Knight Istvan is felled only after Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy has already been defeated, the spell can be found inside the Drawing Room within Volcano Manor. Cast it in enclosed spaces where the explosion reaches more than one body, and hold the button for a boss standing close.
name: Magma Shot
effect: Fire lump of magma that explodes on contact

desc: Sorcery of those who abandoned the practice of incantations after devout faith rewarded them with only despair. Covers the caster in impenetrable thorns grown from the Scadutree. Once covered, dodge rolls will damage enemies. The image of the misshapen Scadutree is an edict: Spurn all that exists. Wound all that exists. For we have been abandoned.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Shadow Keep After draining the water from the Shadow Keep Church District, defeat the Ulcerated Tree Spirit beside a large dead tree.
whatItIs: Wraps the caster in thorns grown from the Scadutree so that every dodge roll carves into nearby enemies. Mantle of Thorns is a sorcery costing 9 FP that needs 20 Faith and no Intelligence. It is a defensive cast with no charge option.
whyItMatters: Turning a dodge into a damage move rewards aggressive spacing around a single boss rather than backing away. Faith-based casters who want a self-sufficient defense without spending a flask can lean on it instead of a shield. The low FP cost means it can be spammed between other casts without draining the pool.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Drain the water from the Shadow Keep Church District, then defeat the Ulcerated Tree Spirit beside a large dead tree to get it. Equip it before any boss fight where dodging through an attack window is part of the plan, and roll toward the enemy to convert the evasion into a hit.
name: Mantle of Thorns
effect: Covers self with the Scadutree's impenetrable thorns

desc: Sorcery originating from the putrid liquor of the stone coffins. Flings a great mass of putrescence that explodes shortly after impact, raining ghostflame upon the area. In an age long past, Death was burned by ghostflame. Even the remains of tainted flesh were given equal treatment in death.
location: Loot: Gravesite Plain (Stone Coffin Fissure) Found in the Stone Coffin Fissure by jumping to a lower ledge near the Fissure Waypoint Site of Grace.
whatItIs: Hurls a heavy mass of putrescence that bursts a moment after impact and rains ghostflame over a wide area. Mass of Putrescence is a sorcery that costs 41 FP and asks for 28 Intelligence plus 22 Faith. It can be charged for a larger blast.
whyItMatters: The delayed explosion and the ghostflame rain make it a strong area-denial tool against enemies that crowd around the caster. High-stat casters who have both Intelligence and Faith trained up will feel the damage land harder. Against bosses that pull in adds, the wide splash can thin the group before the main exchange begins.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Jump to the lower ledge near the Fissure Waypoint Site of Grace in the Stone Coffin Fissure in the Gravesite Plain to find it. Cast it when a group of enemies is closing in or when a boss has just finished a big move and is recovering, so the rain lands while it is exposed.
name: Mass of Putrescence
effect: Flings a great mass of putrescence

desc: An incantation of Messmer the Impaler. Summons Messmer's flame to form a giant floating orb. The orb soars toward a foe, crashes into the earth, and explodes after a brief delay. Charging enhances potency. Messmer despised his own fire. Time and time again he hoped to rid himself of it, but ever did it burn.
location: Trade: Remembrance of the Impaler Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold. The remembrance is acquired by defeating Messmer the Impaler. After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to duplicate it. The spell...
whatItIs: Shapes Messmer's flame into a giant floating orb that soars toward the target, crashes into the ground, and explodes after a short delay. Messmer's Orb is an incantation costing 31 FP in 2 FP slots that needs 60 Faith. It can be charged for more power.
whyItMatters: The long flight time and the delayed explosion make it a setup tool: it forces the target to commit to a dodge or a position, then the blast catches them where they went. Pure Faith builds at high levels will find the raw damage competitive with other heavy-hitting incantations. The two-slot cost means it competes with other Faith options for inventory space.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Defeat Messmer the Impaler to earn the Remembrance of the Impaler, then trade it to Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold to receive it. Use it against large bosses that take a few seconds to reposition, casting when they are mid-attack so the delayed blast catches them as they recover.
name: Messmer's Orb
effect: Shapes Messmer's flame into a giant orb that soars at foe

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries that manipulates gravitational forces. Summons a void that emits a rain of small meteorites. Hold to continue the effect. The sorcery originates from the Onyx Lords, who had skin of stone, and were called lords in reverential fear of their destructive power.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Liurnia of the Lakes Acquired from defeating the Onyx Lord at the Royal Grave Evergaol.
whatItIs: Opens a void above the target that pours down a rain of small meteorites for as long as the button is held. Meteorite is a sorcery costing 30 FP and needing 30 Intelligence. It belongs to the gravity school and rewards holding the cast to extend the shower.
whyItMatters: A sustained area-of-effect that pins enemies under a zone of damage makes it strong against groups that refuse to spread out. Mid-level Intelligence casters get access to it earlier than many heavier sorceries, so it fills the gap before more expensive options unlock. The long cast channel means it rewards positioning: get the enemy under the void and then commit.
whenToUse: It drops from the Onyx Lord at the Royal Grave Evergaol in Liurnia of the Lakes. Equip it once 30 Intelligence is reachable and a caster wants a reliable crowd tool in the mid game. Cast it over groups of enemies in open arenas or over a boss that has just been knocked down, holding the button to extend the rain.
name: Meteorite
effect: Calls small meteors down from the sky

desc: One of the glintstone sorceries that manipulates gravitational forces. Summons a void that emits a hail of meteorites. Hold to continue the effect. A manifestation of the power with which Astel leveled the Eternal City.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Consecrated Snowfield Acquired from defeating the Astel, Stars of Darkness bossfight that lurks at the end of Yelough Anix Tunnel.
whatItIs: Tears a void in the air and drops a heavier hail of meteorites that keeps falling while the cast is held. Meteorite of Astel is a sorcery costing 60 FP in 2 slots and requiring 55 Intelligence. The gravity school spell rewards holding the button to extend the bombardment.
whyItMatters: The sustained damage zone pins enemies in a wide area, making it strong against groups that cluster or against a single boss that cannot leave the kill zone. A high-Intelligence caster in the late base game gets a reliable area tool that does not depend on hitting a single target. The two-slot cost and 60 FP price mean it replaces other sorceries in the loadout rather than sitting alongside them.
whenToUse: It drops from Astel, Stars of Darkness at the end of Yelough Anix Tunnel in the Consecrated Snowfield. Equip it once 55 Intelligence is met and the caster wants a late-game crowd control option. Cast it over a boss that has just launched a projectile, so the enemy is forced to stay in the rain while it recovers.
name: Meteorite of Astel
effect: Calls a hail of small meteorites from the void.

desc: Incantation in praise of Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame. Summons an apparition of the Lord's head to spew frenzied flame. This incantation can be used while in motion. The apparition will remain for as long as the input is held. The Lord of Frenzied Flame shall take their torment, despair. Their affliction. Every sin, every curse. All melted away. Yet Midra, like others before him, was too weak to become a Lord.
location: Trade: Remembrance of the Lord of Frenzied Flame The remembrance is acquired by defeating Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame. Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold. After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to...
whatItIs: An incantation of the Frenzied Flame that calls the Lord's severed head into the air and lets it breathe a torrent of blazing fire forward. It comes from the Shadow of the Erdtree, demands a steep Faith investment, and stays active for the whole duration of the hold while the caster keeps moving.
whyItMatters: A mobile flame stream gives Faith builds a way to deal sustained pressure without committing to a stationary cast. The two-slot cost is worth it when a caster needs to keep moving around an arena while still dealing damage. Against bosses with telegraphed wide attacks, the mobility of the cast makes dodging through the window easier.
whenToUse: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion must be owned before it can be obtained. Defeating Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame yields the Remembrance of the Lord of Frenzied Flame, which Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold will exchange for the incantation. Hold the cast during long engagements against circling foes so the flame tracks them while you keep your distance.
name: Midra's Flame of Frenzy
effect: Summons Lord of Frenzied Flame's head to spew frenzied flame

desc: Secret incantation of Queen Marika. Only the kindness of gold, without Order. Creates a small, illusory Erdtree that continuously restores the HP of nearby allies. Marika bathed the village of her home in gold, knowing full well that there was no one to heal.
location: Loot: Scaduview Found in Shaman Village, under a very, very small Minor Erdtree among a field of golden flowers. The path is guarded by a Tree Sentinel.
whatItIs: Plants a small illusory Erdtree at the target point that continuously restores the HP of any ally standing near it. Minor Erdtree is an incantation costing 30 FP in 2 slots and requiring 70 Faith. It does no damage and exists purely as a healing zone.
whyItMatters: A free, continuous heal removes the need to spend a flask during long boss fights or sustained combat. High-Faith casters who lack a dedicated healing incantation get a reliable safety net without swapping loadouts. In co-op play it supports a partner across the whole fight, reducing their flask pressure.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Travel to the Shaman Village in Scaduview, past the Tree Sentinel that guards the path, and look under a very small Minor Erdtree among a field of golden flowers. Cast it in a safe spot before a boss fight or during a long dungeon run, then fight inside its radius to heal steadily.
name: Minor Erdtree
effect: Continuously heals allies in the area

desc: Sorcery of a preceptor who served the Carian royal family. Used to conceal oneself in a glintstone haze, reappearing after a few seconds have passed. Directional inputs determine where one will reappear. The curator of the study hall was such a master of this sorcery that it now bears her name.
location: Available for purchase from Count Ymir upon first meeting him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. The Twin Maiden Husks sell Miriam's Vanishing if given Ymir's Bell Bearing.
whatItIs: Hides the caster in a glintstone haze for a few seconds, then reappears them wherever the directional inputs point. Miriam's Vanishing is a sorcery costing 9 FP and needing 26 Intelligence. It is a pure evasion tool with no damage component.
whyItMatters: A guaranteed dodge window that ignores the timing of a normal roll gives an escape route when a boss attack is about to connect. Low FP cost means it can be cast on top of other spells without draining the pool. In tight corridors or against multi-hit combos, the repositioning after the vanish can carry the caster to a safe angle.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. Count Ymir sells it upon first meeting him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, or the Twin Maiden Husks will sell it if given Ymir's Bell Bearing. Cast it the instant a boss telegraphs a heavy attack that is about to land, using the directional input to appear behind or beside the target.
name: Miriam's Vanishing
effect: Conceals self in a glintstone haze

desc: Incantation of those who served Miquella. Produces a multilayered golden ring of light and fires it forwards, inflicting continuous damage on those struck by it. Charging increases potency. This light-ring incantation was cultivated by a tradition separate from Golden Order fundamentalism.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Stone Coffin Fissure Defeat the Phantom Misbegotten Warrior found past the Fissure Waypoint Site of Grace along the main path through the area.
whatItIs: A golden ring of layered light that shoots forward and keeps dealing damage to everything it passes through. It is a single-slot incantation tied to the Miquella tradition, asking for a high Faith floor, and holding the cast makes the ring expand to cover a wider arc.
whyItMatters: A beam that hits everything in a straight line makes it strong against rows of enemies or a boss standing in a narrow passage. Mid-Faith casters get a reliable single-target tool that does not require extreme stats to make the damage feel good. The charge option widens the ring and adds potency, making it a strong burst tool against a boss that has just finished a big move.
whenToUse: Found in the Shadow of the Erdtree content, it drops from the Phantom Misbegotten Warrior past the Fissure Waypoint Site of Grace along the main path through the Stone Coffin Fissure. Line it up down long corridors or into a boss during a recovery window, and hold the cast to stretch the ring for a heavier pass.
name: Multilayered Ring of Light
effect: Fires a multilayered golden ring of light that continuously inflicts damage

desc: One of the night sorceries of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. Fires a semi-invisible magic comet. This sorcery can be cast repeatedly and while in motion. Charging enhances potency. The Sellian sorcerers were assassins, and it is said that they often hunted their fellows.
location: Loot: Caelid Acquired from a treasure chest blocked by a magic barrier in the middle of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. To dispel the barrier, light this specific barrier, light the brazier in the southwestern tower of the town.
whatItIs: Launches a semi-invisible comet of night magic that streaks forward and can be fired repeatedly without a long cooldown. Night Comet is a sorcery costing 21 FP and needing 38 Intelligence. It can be cast while moving and charged for more force.
whyItMatters: The ability to fire in succession while strafing makes it a strong dueling tool against a single boss in an open arena. High-Intelligence casters get a fast, responsive projectile that does not require standing still to aim. The semi-invisible trajectory is harder for enemies to read, which makes dodging the shot less reliable for them.
whenToUse: It sits in a treasure chest in the middle of Sellia, Town of Sorcery in Caelid, behind a magic barrier that clears once the brazier in the southwestern tower is lit. Equip it once 38 Intelligence is met and a caster wants a fast, mobile projectile option. Fire it in quick bursts while strafing a boss, and charge the last shot of each burst for a heavier hit.
name: Night Comet
effect: Fires semi-invisible magic comet

desc: One of the night sorceries of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. Releases a life-sapping silver mist before the caster, dealing damage to all caught within, including the caster. This sorcery can be cast while in motion. Below Sellia, the Eternal City of Nokron sleeps. This sorcery originates from the maiden of that place.
location: Purchase: Caelid / Roundtable Hold Sold for 5,000 Runes by Sage Gowry after he has repaired the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle. Should Gowry die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Gowry's...
whatItIs: A silver mist of Sellia that billows forward and leaches life from every target inside it, the caster included. It is a low-Intelligence sorcery that can be loosed mid-stride, and holding the cast stretches the cloud to cover a broader patch of ground.
whyItMatters: The lowest Intelligence requirement among the Night sorceries means an early caster can use it with barely any build investment. The self-damage penalty is the trade-off: standing in the mist costs HP, so the cast must be timed so the enemy is in the cloud and the caster is at its edge. Against groups in tight spaces, the wide coverage makes it a strong cleanup tool.
whenToUse: Sage Gowry sells it for 5,000 Runes after he has repaired the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle, or the Twin Maiden Husks at Roundtable Hold will sell it for the same price if Gowry is dead and his Bell Bearing is turned in. Cast it into a group of enemies in a corridor, then back up to the edge of the mist so the self-damage is minimal while the foes keep taking hits.
name: Night Maiden's Mist
effect: Releases life-sapping silver mist before caster

desc: One of the night sorceries of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. Swiftly fires a semi-invisible projectile. This sorcery can be used without delay after performing another action. The Sellian sorcerers were assassins, and it is said that they often hunted their fellows.
location: Purchase: Caelid / Roundtable Hold Sold for 4,000 Runes by Sage Gowry after he has repaired the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle. Should Gowry die before purchasing this Sorcery from him, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Gowry's...
whatItIs: Sends a fast, semi-invisible shard of night magic that can be fired immediately after another action without a delay. Night Shard is a sorcery costing 7 FP and needing 18 Intelligence. It is a quick, low-cost projectile in the same Night school as the heavier Sellian spells.
whyItMatters: The no-delay property means it can be chained after a dodge, a cast, or a weapon swing, making it a reliable fill-between spell in a caster rotation. The 7 FP cost is the cheapest among the Night sorceries, so it can be spammed in succession without draining the pool. An early-to-mid game caster with 18 Intelligence gets a responsive ranged tool before reaching higher-stat options.
whenToUse: It is available from Sage Gowry for 4,000 Runes once he has fixed the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle, or from the Twin Maiden Husks if that path was missed. Use it as a free shot after dodging or after another cast, and save the heavier Night sorceries for moments when the enemy is committed and less likely to move.
name: Night Shard
effect: Swiftly fires a semi-invisible magic projectile

desc: Ancient power of the Godskin Nobles. Thrust out belly with gusto to produce a shockwave that knocks back nearby foes. Charging enhances potency, knocking enemies into the air. Once a sign of the gods' wrath, this incantation became a trophy of the Nobles' god hunt.
location: Guaranteed Drop: Volcano Manor Noble Presence is acquired by defeating the Godskin Noble found at the Temple of Eiglay on Mt. Gelmir.
whatItIs: Puffs out the caster's belly with gusto to send a shockwave that shoves nearby enemies backward. Noble Presence is an incantation costing 20 FP and needing 26 Faith. Charging it launches the knocked-back enemies into the air for a brief airborne window.
whyItMatters: A close-range burst of knockback breaks an enemy's combo and creates space to reset a fight. Faith-based casters who want a non-damage interrupt can use it to create breathing room without spending a flask. The charged version that launches foes overhead pairs well with follow-up spells or weapon attacks while the target is airborne.
whenToUse: It drops from the Godskin Noble at the Temple of Eiglay on Mt. Gelmir in the Volcano Manor area. Equip it when fighting enemies in tight spaces where a knockback opens up the corridor, and charge the cast to launch a boss into the air before landing a heavy hit while it is airborne.
name: Noble Presence
effect: Thrust out belly with gusto to unleash repelling shockwave

desc: Incantation of the Fire Monks. Momentarily sparks roaring flame from the caster's hand. Charging enhances potency. The Giants' Flame still smolders upon the distant northern mountaintop, and the Fire Monks are its guardians.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants Sold for 6,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Fire Monks' Prayerbook. Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then...
whatItIs: Roaring flame erupts from the open palm in a single sharp flash. It is a Fire Monk incantation that asks for a modest Faith level, and holding the button before release extends the burst into a sustained column.
whyItMatters: The low stat requirement and short cast make it one of the first offensive incantations a new Faith build can rely on. The fire damage type is effective against enemies that are weak to it, and the quick cast means it does not interrupt a rhythm of dodging and striking. It fills the gap between basic melee and the heavier incantations that demand more Faith.
whenToUse: Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows will each sell it for 6,000 Runes after being given the Fire Monks' Prayerbook. Equip it as the first offensive incantation for a Faith build and swap it out once a higher-damage fire spell fits the loadout. Cast it at close range during the recovery of a melee combo, or hold the cast to charge a bigger flame against a boss standing still.
name: O, Flame!
effect: Momentarily sparks roaring flame from hand

desc: Sorcery of the claymen who served as priests in the ancient dynasty. Produces several small magical bubbles that drift towards foes before they naturally pop. Charging increases the delay before the bubbles pop. The claymen search for lost oracles within their bubbles.
location: Siofra River region: in the ruins near the Mistwood entrance (Siofra River Well) to the underground region. It's on top of the large, broken statue. To get to it, head to the next level up in the ruins, then carefully traverse the ruins' beams to get to the area above the statue to drop down on...
whatItIs: Looses several small magical bubbles that drift lazily toward enemies before popping and dealing damage. Oracle Bubbles is a sorcery costing 12 FP and asking for 19 Intelligence plus 15 Arcane. Holding the cast button delays the pop, keeping the bubbles alive longer.
whyItMatters: The slow, drifting trajectory makes it forgiving to aim and effective against enemies that move in wide arcs. The Arcane requirement is unusual for a sorcery, so a build that has trained Arcane for other effects can slot it in without needing high Intelligence. The delayed pop means the bubbles can be cast from range and still land on a target that has shifted position.
whenToUse: The sorcery book sits on top of the large, broken statue in the ruins near the Mistwood entrance by the Siofra River Well. Equip it early when the Intelligence and Arcane bars are in reach and a caster wants a slow, forgiving projectile. Let the bubbles drift into a cluster of enemies from a safe distance, or hold the cast to keep them airborne while lining up a better angle.
name: Oracle Bubbles
effect: Launches several small magic bubbles

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. Used by hunters of Those Who Live in Death. Alleviates death blight buildup. The noble Goldmask lamented what had become of the hunters. How easy it is for learning and learnedness to be reduced to the ravings of fanatics; all the good and the great wanted, in their foolishness, was an absolute evil to contend with. Does such a notion exist in the fundamentals of Order?
location: Guaranteed Drop: Nokron, Eternal City Drops from a Scarab found in the circular room in the southeastern quarter of Siofra Aqueduct, past the Crucible Tree Knight.
whatItIs: Golden Order words that purge death blight buildup from the caster, removing the corruption that would otherwise chip away at health. The incantation needs a touch of both Intelligence and Faith, spends a small amount of FP, and hurts no enemy.
whyItMatters: Death blight is a damage-over-time effect that is hard to remove without a flask, so this incantation gives a clean way to strip it off before it becomes dangerous. A hybrid caster with both stats trained can slot it in without conflicting with their main build. It is a low-cost way to remove the buildup, which matters in areas where death blight is applied constantly.
whenToUse: It drops from a Scarab in the circular room in the southeastern quarter of Siofra Aqueduct in Nokron, Eternal City, past the Crucible Tree Knight. Equip it before entering any area where enemies apply death blight, and cast it the moment the blight meter appears rather than waiting for it to fill.
name: Order Healing
effect: Alleviates death blight buildup

desc: One of the incantations of the Golden Order fundamentalists. Used by hunters of Those Who Live in Death. Enchants armament held in the right hand with holy-affinity attacks. This incantation is especially damaging to Those Who Live in Death. Any felled by this incantation cannot be revived. The role of the hunters is to stamp out defiled reason - all for the perfection of the Golden Order.
location: Purchase: Roundtable Hold Sold by D, Hunter of the Dead for 3,000 Runes after speaking to Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum.
whatItIs: Coats the weapon in the right hand with a holy glow that turns every swing into a holy-affinity strike. Order's Blade is an incantation costing 22 FP and needing 13 Intelligence plus 13 Faith. It hits especially hard against Those Who Live in Death, and any foe it kills cannot be revived.
whyItMatters: A melee buff that adds holy damage to every weapon swing makes it a strong fit for any build that wants a Faith hybrid without committing to pure incantation casting. The no-revive effect is a hard kill that prevents certain enemy types from cycling back in. The low stat requirements mean a mixed build can layer it on top of a physical weapon without over-investing.
whenToUse: D, Hunter of the Dead sells it for 3,000 Runes at Roundtable Hold after speaking to Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum. Cast it before a boss fight where the enemy is a member of Those Who Live in Death, or before any area where undead enemies spawn in groups. Re-cast it after it wears off, and keep a melee weapon equipped at all times while it is active.
name: Order's Blade
effect: Enchanted right-hand armament with holy damage

desc: Incantation of the servants of rot. Secretes countless sticky threads, launching them forwards. A technique of the pale pests who crawl through the lands afflicted by scarlet rot; the abandoned children of the goddess. "Do you have an interest in rot incantations?"
location: Quest Item / Purchase: Gowry's Shack (Caelid) Sold for 7,500 Runes by Sage Gowry after giving Millicent the Valkyrie's Prosthesis.
whatItIs: Spits out a spray of sticky rot threads that fly forward and coat enemies they touch. Pest Threads is an incantation costing 19 FP and needing 11 Faith. The threads are the signature technique of the pale pests that crawl through scarlet-rot lands.
whyItMatters: The low Faith requirement makes it accessible to nearly any build that can equip an incantation. The sticky threads mark and slow enemies, setting up follow-up hits from a weapon or another spell. Against groups in open areas, the wide spray covers more ground than a single-target projectile.
whenToUse: Sage Gowry sells it for 7,500 Runes at his shack in Caelid after the Valkyrie's Prosthesis has been given to Millicent. Equip it for fights in scarlet-rot areas where enemies deal the same affliction back, and cast it into a group before swinging a weapon to land the marked hits.
name: Pest Threads
effect: Launches countless sticky threads before caster

desc: Skill of the pests known as the Kindred of Rot, now wielded as an incantation. Secrete numerous sticky threads, then twist them into two spears launched frontwards. Charge to enhance potency. The pests are abandoned servants, and it is for this reason that they found a mother in the Saint of the Bud.
location: Loot: Ancient Ruins of Rauh From the Rauh Ancient Ruins, West Site of Grace, head west into the ruins and take the elevator up inside of it. Exit the ruins and head across the small body of water to the ruin with Scarlet Rot puddles, and go to the far-left back corner to find the spell.
whatItIs: Shoots numerous sticky threads forward, then twists them into two spears that fly at the target. Pest-Thread Spears is an incantation costing 28 FP and needing 26 Faith. It can be charged for a stronger, more concentrated pair of spears.
whyItMatters: The two-spear pattern covers a wider angle than a single projectile, making it harder for a boss to sidestep both. Faith builds that want a ranged attack with more body than a single bolt get a satisfying mid-range tool. The charge option packs both spears into a denser hit that lands harder on a boss in its recovery pause.
whenToUse: Requires the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. From the Rauh Ancient Ruins, West Site of Grace, head west into the ruins and take the elevator up, then exit and cross the small body of water to the ruin with Scarlet Rot puddles, where it sits in the far-left back corner. Cast it at mid range during a boss recovery, and hold the button to charge the spears for a heavier pair of hits.
name: Pest-Thread Spears
effect: Secrete sticky threads and twist them into two frontward flying spears

desc: Power gleaned from the remembrance of Dragonlord Placidusax. Transforms caster into the Dragonlord to spew golden breath from above. This incantation can be cast while jumping. These are the dying wails of the Dragonlord who once dwelled eternally beyond time.
whatItIs: An incantation that transforms the caster into a draconic form and unleashes a torrent of golden flame from above. It costs 80 FP across three slots and demands 36 Faith. The breath can be cast mid-jump, adding a vertical element to an otherwise ground-level attack.
whyItMatters: The wide sweeping arc hits everything below, making it useful against clustered mobs and large bosses that stay low. A Faith build with enough FP to spare gains a reliable area-damage tool that does not require precise aim.
whenToUse: Cast it when a group of enemies is bunched together or when a large boss fills the screen at close to medium range. It fits the mid-to-late base game, once Faith builds have the points and FP pool to support a three-slot spell.
name: Placidusax's Ruin
effect: Spews golden breath of Dragonlord Placidusax

desc: Incantation of the servants of rot. Enchants armament held in the right hand with poison. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Those who dwell within poison know rot all too well. The death that begets life, that comes to all equally. That is to say: it is the cycle of rebirth put into practice.
location: Guaranteed drop: Caelid Dropped by an invisible Scarab roaming around south of Sellia Crystal Tunnel, along the Swamp of Aeonia. The Scarab is west of the Sellia Under-Stair Site of Grace.
whatItIs: A weapon buff that coats the armament in the right hand with poison. It costs 15 FP for a single slot and needs only 10 Faith, so even a low-faith build can equip it. The enchant can be applied while moving, so it does not interrupt a combo.
whyItMatters: Poison damage ticks independently of the weapon's base damage, which means a modest melee build can still deal meaningful sustained damage to enemies with high physical resistances. Any build that wants extra damage on a weapon without investing heavily in Faith gets a quick option here.
whenToUse: Apply the buff before fighting tough enemies that shrug off physical hits, then go in swinging. It is a guaranteed drop in Caelid, released by an invisible Scarab roaming south of Sellia Crystal Tunnel along the Swamp of Aeonia, just west of the Sellia Under-Stair Site of Grace.
name: Poison Armament
effect: Enchants right-hand armament with poison

desc: Incantation of the servants of rot. Releases a poisonous mist before the caster. This incantation can be cast while in motion. Those who dwell within poison know rot all too well. The death that begets life, that comes to all equally. That is to say: it is the cycle of rebirth put into practice.
